intro:
This collection presents the 16 MBTI personality profiles. Each sheet speaks directly to you: it describes your way of seeing the world, your strengths and your points of vigilance, then your professional, romantic, family and friendship life. It then adds what the MBTI does not say: what the Word of God invites you to do with who you are.

A word of caution. The MBTI is a tool for knowing yourself better. It is not the Bible, and it says nothing about your worth before God. No one fits in four letters. If your portrait resembles you only in part, that is normal: keep what enlightens you and leave the rest.

How to use your sheet

  • Find your type, with a serious test or with the help of people who know you well.
  • Read your whole sheet, starting with your strengths.
  • Choose a single weakness in the table and work on it for a month, with the verses and actions suggested.
  • Also read the sheet of your spouse, your children or your colleagues. You will understand them better.

Whatever your type, you have strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help. Saying “that’s my character, I can’t help it” does not match what the Word says: God completes what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6).

ISTJ.html:
Your portrait

You are calm, reserved, attached to security and a peaceful life. A deep sense of duty gives you a serious air and the strength to carry your tasks through to the end. You work in an organized and methodical way, and you succeed at almost everything you undertake. Faithful and reliable, you value honesty and integrity. People can count on you for the good of your family and your community. You take life seriously, but your humor is offbeat and you know how to have fun, especially with family or colleagues.

You believe in laws, traditions, procedures and plans, and you expect the same from others. You do not like breaking a rule. If your intuitive side is little developed, you may cling to structure and want to do everything by the instructions.

Because you are extremely reliable, you are entrusted with a lot of work, and your sense of duty keeps you from saying no when the load becomes too heavy. You then work long hours and people can take advantage of you without your realizing it. On what you judge important, you spend enormous energy. What makes no sense to you, or whose practical use you do not see, you resist. You prefer to work alone and you insist on being accountable for your actions. Theory and abstract thinking interest you little, unless their use is obvious.

You have an immense respect for facts. An idea different from your point of view demands an effort from you, but you can adopt it if it comes from someone you respect. Once you support a cause, you spare no effort to give it all the support needed. Other people’s feelings, on the other hand, are not your natural ground and you poorly perceive their emotional needs. A perfectionist with yourself, you take others’ efforts for granted, as you take your own.

You are uncomfortable expressing your affection and your emotions. Your sense of duty and your ability to see what must be done nevertheless help you go beyond your reserve. You are kind to those you love, you value family spirit and traditions, and you show your love through actions more than words.

You can take any task, define it, organize it, plan it and carry it through to the end. You are a worker who goes deep. Your home is probably tastefully arranged and impeccably kept: you are sensitive to your environment and you need structure, order and beauty.

Under stress, you can switch into “catastrophe” mode. You see only what is going wrong, you blame yourself for what you should have done differently or what you failed at, you lose your calm and your sense of proportion, and you sink into visions of misfortune.

Overall, your potential is enormous. Capable, logical, reasonable, efficient, you have what it takes to reach the goals you set for yourself, whatever they are.

Your strengths

  • You honor your commitments and you take your role very seriously. For the effort put into relationships, you deserve the gold medal of all the types.
  • You are persevering, organized, reliable and honest. Important tasks are entrusted to you because people know they will be done.
  • You know how to listen and you manage money well, with prudence.
  • You accept constructive criticism well and you tolerate conflict without emotional upheaval. You also know how to criticize when necessary.
  • You are loyal to your family and you care deeply about your loved ones, even if you show it more by your actions than your words.

Your points of vigilance

  • You easily believe you are always right. You may be wrong and yet shake others’ confidence by your assurance.
  • You quickly turn a discussion into a win-lose situation, and you find it hard to see the value of a point of view that does not match the facts as you know them.
  • You perceive little of what others feel and you rarely give enough praise or affection to your loved ones.
  • Your taste for structure can seem rigid to others, and you may cling to instructions to the point of neglecting your intuition.
  • You can’t say no. You wear yourself out at work and people abuse your reliability.
  • Under stress, you scold yourself and see nothing but catastrophe.

Your career

Perseverance is your advantage for succeeding. You are at your best in a field where you can use your organizational skills and your ability to bring order and structure. You excel in managing and administering a business.

The jobs that suit you: business executive, administrator, manager, accountant, financial officer, police officer or detective, judge, lawyer, doctor or dentist, programmer or systems analyst, military leader.

You in love

You honor your commitments. Once you have said yes, you are bound to the relationship until death and you take your vows very seriously. You take on your responsibilities as a spouse and parent as best you can. If healthy relationships are among your goals, you do everything to nurture them. You approach the relationship in a very traditional and structured way. You also express your love through physical intimacy, fairly regularly, but you find it hard to say your deepest feelings and to show warmth.

Faced with a disagreement, you first try to convince the other, persuaded that they are simply missing the facts. You base your opinions on what is known, so you hardly see the value of another point of view. The conversation quickly turns into a win-lose match, which weighs especially on intimacy. Yet you do not feel threatened by constructive criticism or by conflict.

You decide rationally, so you think little about others’ feelings. This is a problem if your spouse is a Feeling (F) type. Remember that others need to hear that they are loved and appreciated, even if you yourself do not need it. When an emotional need is pointed out to you as important, you add it to your task list and get seriously to work on it, which makes you a precious companion. Your natural partners are ESFPs or ESTPs.

You as a parent

You are a faithful and devoted parent. You expect your children to respect traditional family roles and you demand respect. You consider it your duty to teach them when they have done wrong and, if necessary, to punish. You often forget to praise them. You create a safe and consistent environment for them, with clear roles and limits. This can sometimes create a gap, especially in adolescence, but they will eventually thank you for having always done your best and put their needs before your own.

You as a friend

Friendship is not your first priority, but you bond with people who have interests and points of view close to yours. You live seriously, and you also know how to have fun and let go. You like the company of optimistic extraverts, even if their enthusiasm sometimes gets on your nerves. You get along with most types and you forge strong bonds with other xSxJs. Your respect for laws and traditions complicates relationships with Perceiving (P) types. You get along rather well with intuitives, even if you do not always understand their point of view.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your faithfulness is precious to God: “Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.” (1 Corinthians 4:2).
  • Your perseverance carries you: “Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.” (Galatians 6:9).
  • Your integrity gives you assurance: “He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.” (Proverbs 10:9).
  • Your concern for family is a calling: “As for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh” (Joshua 24:15).
  • Your love that goes through actions has a biblical basis: “My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.” (1 John 3:18).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You think you are right and you turn the discussion into a tug of war.Proverbs 12:15: the fool’s way is right in his own eyes, but the wise listens to counsel. / Philippians 2:3-4: look also to the interests of others. / James 1:19: quick to listen, slow to speak.Before answering, restate what the other has just said. Ask yourself: “What if I were wrong?” Seek agreement, not victory.
You poorly perceive others’ emotions and compliment little.Romans 12:15: rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep. / 1 Thessalonians 5:11: encourage one another and build one another up. / Proverbs 25:11: a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold.Put encouragement on your task list: one sincere compliment a day. Ask “how are you feeling?” and listen without correcting.

Set a real day of rest each week. Learn to say: “I can’t take this on top of everything else.”

Try a new method each month. Listen to the intuitives around you.

When you reproach yourself for something, tell God instead of ruminating on it. Ask for help before you are at the end of your rope.
You are demanding with your children and praise them little.Ephesians 6:4: bring up your children in the Lord. / Colossians 3:21: do not provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged. / Hebrews 12:11: discipline yields the fruit of peace.For every correction, find two things to approve. Tell each child what you admire in them. Explain your rules instead of imposing them.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say your feelings out loud, even if it costs you. Your actions speak, but your spouse also needs words (Proverbs 25:11).
  • As a parent, keep your solid framework and add tenderness to it: “Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.” (Colossians 3:21).
  • As a friend, you can make your faithfulness a witness: “Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works” (Hebrews 10:24).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Set a precise time for the Word and prayer every day. Your taste for regularity will be an asset here (Psalm 1:2).
  • Sincerely compliment one person a day, in person or in writing.
  • Take a real day of rest each week, without work or a task list.
  • Before defending your opinion, listen to the other to the end and restate what they said.
  • Each evening, note one fact in which God was faithful to you (Lamentations 3:22-23).

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for making me faithful, reliable and attached to what is right. Teach me to listen before convincing, to say my love with words as with actions, to rest in you and not to carry alone what does not belong to me. Keep me from rigidity and open my heart to what you are doing anew. Amen.

ESTJ.html:
Your portrait

You live in a world of facts and concrete needs, anchored in the present. You honor traditions and laws, and you have a clear set of standards and beliefs. You expect the same from others and you poorly understand those who do not value these systems. You appreciate competence and efficiency, you like to see quick results for your efforts, and you have a clear idea of how things should be.

You are confident, and sometimes offensive. You are very gifted at planning and at seeing what steps to take to accomplish a specific task. You can be very demanding and critical, because your convictions are firmly rooted, and you say what you think bluntly when someone does not meet your standards. At least, people can take you at your word: you are honest.

You are generally a model citizen and a pillar of the community. You take your commitments seriously and you follow to the letter your own idea of good citizenship. You like being with people and having fun, and you can be very loud at parties.

Watch your tendency to be too rigid and too attached to detail. Because you give great weight to your beliefs, think about valuing the contribution and opinions of others. If you neglect your Feeling side, you can hurt by applying reason to situations that call for more sensitivity.

Under stress, you often feel isolated and misunderstood. You who usually talk a lot then find it hard to put words on what you feel and to say it to others.

You place social order above everything and you feel obliged to do what you can to serve it. You mow the lawn, you vote, you attend meetings, you do everything to strengthen personal and social security. You are conscientious, practical, realistic and reliable.

Your strengths

  • You are enthusiastic, optimistic and friendly.
  • You are stable and reliable, and you make great efforts to fulfill your duties and obligations.
  • You take care of practical concerns and you manage money well, with prudence.
  • You do not feel threatened by conflict or criticism, and you prefer to resolve a conflict rather than ignore it.
  • You take your commitments very seriously and you seek lasting relationships.
  • You know how to punish when necessary.

Your points of vigilance

  • You easily believe you are always right and you need to lead.
  • You grow impatient with inefficiency and carelessness, and you have little patience with those who see things differently.
  • You poorly perceive what others feel, you find it hard to express your own emotions, and you can hurt without meaning to by your language.
  • You can become materialistic and too sensitive to social status.
  • You can be too rigid and too attached to detail.

Your career

You will be happiest in a leadership position. Jobs that require creating order and structure suit you best.

The jobs that suit you: military leader, business administrator or manager, police officer or detective, judge, financial officer, teacher, sales representative.

You in love

You seek stability and security. Once you have committed, it is permanent. You are enthusiastic, driven to fulfill your obligations, especially toward your family, and you consider that your relationships are made to last. You have little patience with those who see things differently.

You are the guardian of your family. Your partner appreciates your efforts, but may also feel a degree of control. You may consider it your duty to teach them how to behave or what attitude to adopt. Conversely, you freely give your approval when you are happy or impressed. Positive or negative, your expression is taken at face value, because you are frank.

In intimacy, you are robust, enthusiastic and athletic, rather traditional, and you expect fairly regular relations. You experience them as a physical experience of closeness more than as a moment to express and receive affection.

You like spending time with others and you want your partner to take part in these activities, especially those linked to family, work or an organization. You appreciate being thanked. Because you are little in tune with what others feel, this can be a problem with Feeling types. Your natural partners are ISTPs or INTPs.

You as a parent

You take your responsibilities as a parent seriously and you see it as a natural state. You help your children become responsible and independent adults. You expect respect and honor from them and you tolerate no deviation from this basic rule, nor disorder, nor repeated mistakes. Times can be hard if your children are intuitive or Perceiving types: you are very practical, you poorly understand the creative imagination of intuitive children and you have little patience with the unstructured attitude of P children. Remember that what is good for you is not necessarily good for them.

Whatever the difficulties, you see your role as an obligation. Your children consider you reliable, rigorous, traditional and always ready to sacrifice yourself for their good.

You as a friend

Your family comes first. You still like having fun with others, especially those who share your interests and activities, preferably sports. You have a high sense of social status and you respect those who have risen high on the social ladder. You have little patience with frivolous or non-traditional people, and the types who live in the moment (xSxP) may conversely find your judgments too traditional. You bond with any type when you have a common interest or goal. You like hearing and telling good jokes. Your friends find you reliable, optimistic and easy to draw into various activities.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your sense of leadership is a gift: “he who rules, with diligence” (Romans 12:8).
  • Your stability and reliability bear fruit: “Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.” (1 Corinthians 15:58).
  • Your talent for planning is biblical: “The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.” (Proverbs 21:5). Jesus himself speaks of sitting down to count the cost before building (Luke 14:28).
  • Your frankness has its place when turned toward the good: “speaking truth in love” (Ephesians 4:15).
  • Your role as guardian of your family has a solid basis: “Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labor in vain” (Psalm 127:1).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You think you are always right and you need to lead.Proverbs 12:15: the wise listens to counsel. / Mark 10:43-44: whoever wants to be great will be the servant. / 1 Peter 5:3: lead without lording it over others, as an example.Before any important decision, ask the opinion of two people different from you. Ask yourself: “Am I serving, or am I controlling?” Thank those who contradict you respectfully.
You grow impatient with inefficiency and with those who see things differently.Ephesians 4:2: bear with one another with humility, gentleness and patience. / Proverbs 14:29: one who is slow to anger has great understanding. / Galatians 5:22: patience is a fruit of the Spirit.Before reacting, breathe and ask yourself why the person did it that way. Set a delay before any remark. Say first what is well done, then what needs correcting.
Your language hurts without your meaning it to.Proverbs 12:18: the tongue of the wise brings healing. / Proverbs 15:1: a gentle answer turns away wrath. / Ephesians 4:29: good words that build up.Before voicing a criticism, check: is it true, helpful, said with love? Ask afterward: “How did you take what I said?” Apologize quickly when you have hurt.
You express your feelings poorly and feel misunderstood under stress.Romans 12:15: weep with those who weep. / Psalm 62:8: pour out your heart before God. / 1 Peter 5:7: cast all your worries on him.Name your emotions to God aloud each day. Choose a trusted friend to talk to when you are under pressure. Ask your spouse how they feel, then listen without correcting.
You are drawn to social status and material possessions.Matthew 6:19-21: where your treasure is, there your heart will be. / Luke 12:15: life does not consist in possessions. / James 2:1-4: do not show partiality between rich and poor.Give regularly and discreetly (Matthew 6:3). Honor, by your attention, people without status. Examine your spending and your judgments in the light of these texts.
You demand a lot of your children and poorly understand those who are different from you.Ephesians 6:4: do not provoke your children. / Colossians 3:21: so that they won’t be discouraged. / Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go.Observe each of your children and note what is unique to them. Welcome their ideas before correcting them. Praise them every day for one specific thing.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, replace instructions with questions. Voice your approval as often as your criticism (Ephesians 4:29).
  • As a parent, keep your standards and add gentleness to them: “Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.” (Colossians 3:21).
  • As a friend, serve without dominating. “In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another” (Romans 12:10).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Begin each day with the Word and prayer, before lists and calls.
  • Listen to one person without interrupting and without correcting, at least once a day.
  • Before criticizing, pass your message through the filter: true, helpful, said with love.
  • Express to God what you feel, then say it to someone close.
  • Each week, give time or money to someone who cannot repay you.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for making me organized, reliable and ready to serve. Teach me patience with those who move forward differently from me. May my words heal and not hurt. Give me the courage to say what I feel and the gentleness to listen to what others are going through. Make me a servant and not a heartless boss. Amen.

ISFJ.html:
Your portrait

You are truly warm and caring, and you believe in the goodness of people. You love harmony and cooperation, and you are very sensitive to the feelings of others. People appreciate you because you bring out the best in everyone.

Your inner world is rich, but observers do not always see it. You regularly check in on the people who matter to you. Your memory is exceptional for everything touching your values: you can remember the precise detail of a facial expression or a conversation years later, if the event marked you.

You like security, kindness, respect for traditions and laws. You do not like doing things differently, unless someone explains why the new method is more effective than the old one. You learn better by practice than by reading or theory, and traditional higher education, very abstract, is a chore for you. Once the task is learned, you apply it tirelessly to its end, and you are extremely reliable.

Your home is functional and nicely furnished, and you would make a very good interior decorator. Thanks to your sensitivity to others, you find just the right gift to please.

More than other types, you are very aware of your own feelings as well as those of others. You rarely express yours and you keep them inside. When they are negative, they can pile up until they become firm and irreversible decisions. Some ISFJs nevertheless learn to express them.

You take your responsibilities very seriously, so people naturally count on you. You find it hard to say no and you can end up overloaded. You then do not talk about your difficulties, because you do not like conflict and you place others’ needs before your own.

You need positive feedback. Without it, or in the face of criticism, you get discouraged and can even sink into depression. In stress or difficult situations, you tend to lose confidence in yourself. At heart, you are warm, generous and reliable.

Your strengths

  • You are warm and friendly, and you like to help and to please.
  • You know how to listen and you fulfill your duties and obligations.
  • You have excellent organizational skills and you handle practical matters and daily needs well.
  • You manage money well, with prudence.
  • You take your commitments seriously and you seek lasting relationships.
  • You have a sense of space and aesthetics, which gives you a real talent for practical artistic projects.

Your points of vigilance

  • You do not pay enough attention to your own needs, and you do not express them, which feeds frustrations.
  • You resist change.
  • You like neither conflict nor criticism, and you hold back your feelings until you explode.
  • You find it hard to leave a bad relationship and to turn the page when a relationship ends.
  • You lose confidence in yourself under criticism or stress, and you need others’ approval.
  • You hold yourself responsible for the difficulties of your grown-up children.

Your career

Ideally, you choose a career where you can observe people to understand what they want or need, then use your organizational talent to create a plan or an environment that meets it. Your sense of space and aesthetics also gives you abilities in practical artistic projects such as interior decorating or clothing design.

The jobs that suit you: decorator, designer, nurse, administrator or manager, administrative assistant, childcare worker, social worker, shopkeeper, accountant, home economics.

You in love

You are very committed in your relationships and your feelings are very strong, even if others do not see it, because you keep everything inside. You are faithful and loyal, sometimes to the point of staying faithful to a deceased partner. You are very generous, which can backfire on you if people take advantage of you. You then suppress your feelings and nurse strong resentments.

In intimacy, you see physical relations as a concrete way to strengthen the bond, and almost as a duty. You seek to satisfy your partner more than yourself. You express your love little with words, but a lot through your actions. The finest gift anyone can give you is your partner’s expression of love and gratitude.

You do not like conflict. You say nothing until you have been pushed to the limit, then you explode in anger and say things you later regret. You have a traditional family spirit and the well-being of your loved ones comes first. Your natural partner is the ESTP or ESFP.

You as a parent

For you, being a parent is a natural state and a duty. You care for your children and you teach them the rules of society so that they become responsible and independent adults. Punishing makes you uncomfortable, but you get past this discomfort because you consider it your duty to pass on healthy values. You create well-defined boundaries and roles in the family.

You handle the situation poorly when your children grow up and meet difficulties. You easily believe that you are responsible and that you did not work hard enough. This is generally not the case. In many respects, you are an ideal parent: your children will lack for nothing.

You as a friend

You put your family before everything, but you like spending time with your friends and colleagues. You need to talk before making a decision, and this often goes through your friends. You enjoy the company of most types. You open up little, but you need a few close confidants. You find them preferably among the xSFJs, or, to a lesser extent, the xNFJs. Your friends appreciate you for your warmth, your reliability, the depth of your conscience and your emotional understanding.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your warmth and your service reflect Christ: “through love be servants to one another” (Galatians 5:13).
  • Your reliability is recognized by God: “Well done, good and faithful servant” (Matthew 25:21).
  • Your sensitivity to others brings real comfort: “a kind word makes it glad” (Proverbs 12:25).
  • Your hospitality is a ministry: “contributing to the needs of the saints; given to hospitality” (Romans 12:13).
  • Your sense of aesthetics comes from God, who filled Bezalel with wisdom “to devise skillful works” (Exodus 31:3-4).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You can’t say no, you overload yourself and you forget your needs.Matthew 22:39: love your neighbor as yourself. / Mark 6:31: Jesus invites his disciples to rest. / Galatians 1:10: serve Christ rather than please people.Before accepting, say: “Let me check my schedule and I’ll get back to you tomorrow.” Note what you do for yourself each week. Take real rest without feeling guilty.
You keep your feelings in, then explode in anger.Ephesians 4:26: do not let the sun go down on your anger. / Proverbs 27:5: open rebuke is better than hidden love. / Philippians 4:6: make your needs known to God.Tell God your needs each day, then a trusted person. Speak up as soon as you are bothered, with simple words: “That hurt me.” Do not let resentment settle in.
You need others’ approval and criticism discourages you.Proverbs 29:25: fear of man is a snare. / Romans 8:31: if God is for us, who can be against us? / Colossians 3:23-24: work for the Lord and not for men.When you are criticized, separate what is true from what is hurtful. Reread each week what God says about you. Seek the Lord’s approval first.
You resist change.Isaiah 43:18-19: God does a new thing. / Philippians 3:13-14: forgetting what lies behind, reaching forward to what lies ahead. / Joshua 1:9: be strong, the Lord is with you.Ask “why” before refusing a change. Try one new thing a month. Commit each change to God in prayer.
You find it hard to leave a bad relationship or to turn the page.Psalm 147:3: God heals the brokenhearted. / Hebrews 12:15: see that no root of bitterness springs up. / Ephesians 4:31-32: put away bitterness and forgive.Talk to a trusted counselor or pastor. Write down what you lost and lay it before God. Forgive by decision, even when the feeling is slow to come.
You feel responsible for everything that happens to your children.1 Corinthians 3:6-7: one plants, another waters, but God gives the growth. / Psalm 127:3: children are a heritage from the Lord. / 1 Peter 5:7: cast all your worries on him.Do your part faithfully, then entrust the rest to God. Pray every day for each of your children. Recognize that they have their own path.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say your needs before piling them up. The love you show through your actions is completed by words (Ephesians 4:15).
  • As a parent, keep your tenderness and dare to punish when necessary: “You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.” (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, let others serve you too. “Bear one another’s burdens” applies both ways (Galatians 6:2).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Take a moment with God each day to tell him everything you hold back, without filtering.
  • Say one respectful no a week, and one “I need” a week.
  • Write down three things God says about you, and reread them when criticism touches you.
  • Choose a close confidant and open up to them regularly.
  • Set aside each week a time of rest and a time for a project that gives you pleasure (decorating, sewing, cooking).

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me a heart attentive to others. Teach me to say no when I need to rest, to express what I feel before it overflows, and to seek your approval first. Help me trust your hand in changes and for my children. May my service remain a joy and not a burden. Amen.

ESFJ.html:
Your portrait

You love people. Your sensitivity serves you to gather precise and detailed information about others, and you want to bring out the best in them. You read and understand people’s points of view very well. Your desire to be appreciated makes you pleasant, and people like your company because you have the gift of making everyone feel good about themselves.

You take your responsibilities very seriously. You like security and stability, you are warm and full of energy. You need others’ approval to feel good, you suffer from indifference and you do not understand meanness. You are very generous: your satisfaction comes above all from the happiness of others. You want to be appreciated for who you are and for what you give. Caring, you sometimes find it hard to see or accept a hard truth about someone who matters to you.

You have firm ideas about how things should be, and you do not hesitate to express them. Your moral code is often defined by the community where you live more than by deeply felt inner values. You respect laws and authority and you think others should do the same. You are traditional and you prefer to do things the established way rather than go into unknown territory. This can lead you to accept rules without questioning or understanding them.

ESFJs raised in a solid system of ethical values are often the most generous souls. Without this support, you risk developing questionable values and finding many reasons to justify a fault you want to commit. Your outward-turned Feeling then pushes you to control and manipulate, and your lack of intuition keeps you from stepping back to see the real consequences of your actions. You nevertheless believe you are following a solid moral code. You can also concentrate so much on the desire to please that you become too sensitive and imagine bad intentions where there are none.

You have a natural tendency to want to control your environment. Your dominant function calls for structure and organization, you are more at ease in structured settings, and you do not like theoretical concepts. Be careful with those who do not want to be controlled, such as INTPs and INTJs.

With a good value system, you are warm, sympathetic, helpful, cooperative, concrete, consistent, organized, enthusiastic and energetic. You value tradition and security, and you seek a stable life, rich in contacts with your friends and family.

Your strengths

  • You make great efforts to fulfill your duties and obligations.
  • You are warm, friendly and service-minded: you want to please.
  • You take your commitments very seriously and you seek lasting relationships.
  • You are practical and you are a very good manager of funds.
  • You are optimistic and popular: people are drawn to you.
  • You are family-oriented and you gladly organize family celebrations.

Your points of vigilance

  • You are uncomfortable with change.
  • You have an extreme aversion to conflict and criticism, which you experience as an attack on your whole person.
  • You need a lot of affection to feel good, and you give great importance to others’ opinion of you.
  • You find it hard to accept the end of a relationship and you carry on your shoulders the responsibility for the failure.
  • You have difficulty accepting negative things about those close to you.
  • You do not pay enough attention to your own needs, and you may manipulate to get what you want.

Your career

You are very organized and you like order. A large part of your satisfaction comes from what you bring to others.

The jobs that suit you: home economics, caregiving, teaching, administration, childcare, family doctor, social worker, accountant, administrative assistant.

You in love

You take great care of the people with whom you share an intimate relationship. You take your commitments very seriously: once you have said yes, you make every effort to fulfill your obligations. You are excellent at domestic matters, you take care of daily needs and you are prudent with money.

You want to be appreciated for who you are and for what you give. Sometimes this goes as far as an intense emotional need, which makes you constantly look for signs of affection if they are not given freely. You handle conflict and criticism poorly, and you take any remark as an accusation against your whole personality. Without positive feedback or in the face of negative feedback, you can become depressed. You are also very aware of your social status and of what others think. Make sure this does not disturb your intimate relationship.

In intimacy, you are warm and affectionate. You see it as an opportunity to express your affection and to receive signs of love, and you place great importance on making your partner happy. You have a strong need to belong to institutions, traditions or a family circle. You like taking part in parties or organizing them and you want your spouse to share your social experiences. Your natural partner is the ISFP, or the INFP to another degree.

You as a parent

You are very attached to your role as a parent and you express a lot of love to your children. You expect them to obey. You create a structured environment where boundaries are well defined, with an emphasis on tradition and security. It is hard for you to punish, and you may do so in a less visible way, through manipulation.

Your children will probably rebel at some point, which will be a stressful period for the family. Your natural tendency is then to make them feel guilty, which can seriously damage your relationship.

You as a friend

You put your family before your friends, but you give enormous importance to your friendships. Some of your tendencies can complicate them: you do not always give freely and you often expect something in return, you poorly accept the negative aspects of your loved ones, and you may manipulate. Despite everything, people appreciate you for your warmth and kindness, and for your ability to see the best in others. You generally have a fairly high number of very close friends, of all types.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your generosity is blessed: “The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.” (Proverbs 11:25).
  • Your talent for bringing out the best in others is a ministry of building up: “Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.” (1 Thessalonians 5:11).
  • Your sense of welcome and celebration is a service: “Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.” (1 Peter 4:9).
  • Your practical sense and organization serve God: “Let all things be done decently and in order.” (1 Corinthians 14:40).
  • Your faithfulness in duties is precious: “He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.” (Luke 16:10).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You need others’ approval and the way they look at you.Galatians 1:10: seek to please God rather than men. / John 12:43: loving the glory of men more than the glory of God. / Zephaniah 3:17: God rejoices over you.When you seek a sign of approval, ask yourself: “Whom am I trying to please?” Reread each day a word of God’s love for you. Do good without being seen.
You control, make people feel guilty or manipulate to get what you want.Matthew 5:37: let your yes be yes and your no, no. / 2 Corinthians 4:2: renounce craftiness. / Colossians 3:21: do not provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.Say directly what you want and what you feel, without detours. When you catch yourself making someone feel guilty, stop and rephrase it as a clear request. Ask forgiveness when you have manipulated.
Your values come mostly from your community, and you accept rules without questioning them.Romans 12:2: do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed. / Acts 17:11: the Bereans examined the Scriptures daily. / Proverbs 3:5-6: trust in the Lord with all your heart.Read the Bible yourself and ask: “Does this come from the Word, or only from a habit?” Base your values on Scripture more than on the opinion of your environment.
You find it hard to see or say a hard truth about a loved one, and you experience criticism as rejection.Proverbs 27:6: faithful are the wounds of a friend. / Galatians 6:1: restore with a spirit of gentleness. / Proverbs 9:8: rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.Tell yourself that correcting someone with love is a way of loving them. When you are criticized, ask: “What is true in this?” Thank the person for their candor.
You give while expecting something in return.Luke 6:35: do good, expecting nothing in return. / Matthew 6:3-4: don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does. / Acts 20:35: it is more blessed to give than to receive.Give once a week without expecting thanks. Hand over to God the need to be recognized. When you feel frustrated at receiving nothing, say so simply.
You do not take care of your needs and you handle change poorly.Mark 6:31: Jesus invites his disciples to rest. / Isaiah 43:19: God does a new thing. / Philippians 4:6: make your needs known to God.Take time for yourself each week. Say a need aloud. Accept one small change a month and note what it brought you.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, ask for what you need rather than seeking it through detours. Say things simply and with love (Ephesians 4:15).
  • As a parent, keep your tenderness and replace guilt-tripping with clear explanations: “You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.” (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, learn to give freely and to say a hard truth gently (Galatians 6:1).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Read the Bible every day and note what is God’s command and what is only a habit of your environment.
  • Once a week, do a discreet service that no one knows about.
  • Tell a loved one a hard truth, gently, whenever it is necessary.
  • When you feel criticized, wait an hour before answering and pray.
  • Set aside time each week for your own needs: rest, leisure, friendship.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me a heart that loves people and wants to see them happy. Teach me to seek your approval rather than that of others. Keep me from controlling or manipulating, and give me the courage to tell the truth gently. May my values be anchored in your Word. Help me give freely, without expecting anything in return. Amen.

ISTP.html:
Your portrait

You understand very well how things work. Your reasoning is strong, even though you take an interest in theories and concepts only when you see a practical application for them.

You have an adventurous mind: motorbikes, planes, skydiving, surfing. You love action, you are fiercely independent, and your taste for adventure makes you get bored fairly quickly.

You are faithful to your causes and your beliefs, and you think everyone deserves fairness and justice. You do not always respect the rules of the “system,” but you follow your own rules and guidelines, and you refuse to take part in what violates your personal laws. You are extremely loyal to your “brothers.”

You need time alone to put your head back in order: you absorb the facts of the outside world and you sort them when you are alone.

Pragmatic, you like doing things. Staying behind a desk all day planning for the long term is not for you. Adaptable and spontaneous, you respond to what comes. You have strong technical skills and you can be an excellent technical leader, attentive to detail and to the concrete.

You avoid judging by personal values. For you, decisions must be impartial and based on facts. You pay little attention to the effect you have on others, and you pay little attention to your own feelings. You are wary of them, you even try to ignore them, because you poorly distinguish an emotional reaction from a value judgment. This can be a problem for you.

Stressed, you can explode in anger or be overwhelmed by emotions that you then feel obliged to share.

You are happiest when you are immersed in concrete tasks that require detailed analysis and technical skills. You are optimistic, good-humored, faithful to your peers, simple in your desires, generous and confident.

Your strengths

  • You know how to listen, you are self-confident, optimistic and fun.
  • You are realistic and practical.
  • You fear neither conflict nor criticism.
  • You bounce back quickly when a relationship ends.
  • You know how to punish when necessary, even if you do not feel like it.
  • You respect others’ need for space and privacy.
  • You are gifted at almost everything that interests you, and very loyal to your friends.

Your points of vigilance

  • You find it hard to commit for the long term.
  • You find it hard to express your feelings and emotions, and you are too reserved.
  • You perceive little of what others feel.
  • You need a lot of personal space and you handle being crowded poorly.
  • You get bored quickly and you may forget to invest in your family’s daily life.
  • Under stress, you can explode.

Your career

You are gifted for different types of tasks. Your Introversion and Thinking preference allows you to concentrate and work on very large problems. To be happy, you need great autonomy. Your natural interest goes toward applying your excellent reasoning to practical questions.

The jobs that suit you: police officer or detective, forensic doctor, programmer or systems analyst, engineer, carpenter, mechanic, pilot or motorcycle rider, athlete, entrepreneur.

You in love

You can be very intense and exciting. You live almost entirely in the present moment and you do not commit beyond the immediate future. If a relationship interests you and meets your needs, you do your part to keep it strong and healthy. You hate routine, strict schedules and orders, and you need to keep your space in the couple. You take your commitments day by day: when you say yes, it often means “I’m doing it for now.” You can nevertheless have lasting relationships.

You are sensual, spontaneous, creative, sensitive to aesthetics, and you experience intimacy more as a physical act than as an expression of love and affection.

You hold back your point of view. You like listening to others’ opinions without giving yours, and you often answer a question with another question, which can be frustrating. Your decision-making is entirely internal, so you do not feel the need to share your ideas. In an intimate relationship, you protect yourself even more: you are afraid of facing your deep feelings, you are very vulnerable about them and you build a wall around your heart.

Even if you show nothing, your feelings are often intense. You can feel an irresistible love for your spouse while expressing it little or poorly. You can also feel very in love one day and totally uninterested the next, which others misunderstand. Committing for the long term takes you out of your comfort zone. Those who do so nevertheless discover that one can enjoy a strong, committed relationship while living in the present. Your natural partner is the ESTJ, or, to a lesser extent, the ENTJ.

You as a parent

You are relaxed, flexible, and you take things as they come. Your aversion to control extends to your children: you give them a lot of room to develop. When discipline is necessary, you know how to punish without too much difficulty.

You tend to keep a certain distance. You do not feel a great need to pass on your values or to influence their decisions, and you count on your spouse to create a structured framework. You are relatively little affected by the events of daily family life. You like spending time with them outdoors, fishing, sailing or hunting. It is in these moments of yours that you get to know their point of view.

You as a friend

Your enthusiastic and almost childlike approach to life makes you endearing. You are relaxed and open-minded, which makes you a precious friend and confidant. Your friends share your taste for physical or outdoor activities, such as skiing or swimming. You have little interest and patience for those who do not share your interests. You poorly understand intuitives and you spend little time with them, unless you have a common hobby. You like the company of extraverts for their enthusiasm and spirit, but you end up getting tired of them.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your technical skill is honored: “Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.” (Proverbs 22:29).
  • Your sense of justice is a calling: “He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?” (Micah 6:8).
  • Your loyalty to your brothers joins that of the true friend: “A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.” (Proverbs 18:24).
  • Your confidence and your lack of fear have a source: “Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?” (Psalm 27:1).
  • Your good humor does good: “A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.” (Proverbs 17:22). Your generosity pleases God: “God loves a cheerful giver” (2 Corinthians 9:7).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

Choose a precise and lasting commitment (marriage, service, volunteering) and keep it. Ask God for perseverance.
You have a wall around your heart and you express your feelings poorly.1 John 4:18: perfect love casts out fear. / Psalm 62:8: pour out your heart before God. / Ephesians 4:15: speak the truth in love.Tell God each day what you feel. Choose one person and share one feeling a week. Tell your spouse what you feel for them, even if it seems obvious to you.
You perceive little of what others feel.Romans 12:15: weep with those who weep. / Philippians 2:4: look also to the interests of others. / Proverbs 20:5: a man of understanding draws out the purposes of another’s heart.Ask a question about what the other is going through, then listen without looking for a solution. Use your sense of observation to notice the mood of those around you.
Under stress, you can explode or be overwhelmed.Ephesians 4:26: be angry, and do not sin. / Proverbs 29:11: a wise man keeps his passions in check. / James 1:19-20: slow to anger.Speak before the pressure rises, rather than waiting for the explosion. Walk or exercise to release the tension, then pray. Apologize quickly if you have hurt someone.
You stay distant from your family and you count on your spouse for structure.Deuteronomy 6:6-7: teach the Word to your children. / Ephesians 6:4: bring them up in the Lord. / Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go.Use your outdoor outings to talk about your faith and your values. Take part in one moment of daily family life each day. Share responsibility for discipline with your spouse.
You struggle with rules and authority, and you get bored quickly.Romans 13:1: submit to the authorities. / Ephesians 5:21: submit to one another. / Philippians 4:11-12: learn to be content.Ask yourself the reason for a rule before rejecting it. Seek your adventure in service rather than in risk. Learn to stay faithful, even when enthusiasm drops.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, make your commitment visible: say it, keep it, and let your spouse into your inner world (Matthew 19:6).
  • As a parent, be present and pass on your faith during your outings: “you shall teach them diligently to your children” (Deuteronomy 6:7).
  • As a friend, you are faithful. Also make room for those who do not share your passions (Philippians 2:4).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Spend ten minutes with God in the middle of nature, to pray and read a psalm.
  • Say one feeling a day aloud to someone, even a single word.
  • Each day ask someone a question about what they are going through, and listen to the whole answer.
  • Take on a lasting commitment (church service, mentoring) and keep it for a year.
  • Organize one outing a month with your children and share with them a value or a passage of the Word.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for making me skillful, courageous and loyal. Teach me to keep my commitments and to open my heart to those I love. Deliver me from the fear of being vulnerable. Help me listen to what others feel and stay present for my family. May my sense of justice serve your kingdom. Amen.

ESTP.html:
Your portrait

You are enthusiastic, an “actor” who lives in the world of action. You take risks and you are ready to get your hands dirty. You live here and now and you give little importance to introspection or theory. You decide quickly what must be done, you act and you move on.

You have a strange ability to perceive the attitudes and motivations of others. You pick up small clues that escape most types, such as facial expressions and posture, and you are generally one step ahead of the person in front of you. For you, rules and laws are guidelines, and you can set them aside if necessary. You have your own idea of what is right and what is wrong.

You talk fast and you like the good things in life. You can be a gambler or a spender. You improvise very well and you do things as you go rather than following a plan. You like having fun and people like your company. You can sometimes hurt without knowing it, because your decision-making does not take people’s feelings into account. It is not that you do not care about them: you decide on the basis of facts and logic.

Your intuition is your least developed side. You quickly grow impatient with theories, you see little use for them in getting things done, and you distrust your instinct as much as that of others. School is often hard for you, especially overly theoretical higher studies. You can be intelligent and still find it a pain.

You need to keep progressing in your career. Routine tasks stifle you and make you unhappy. You have a natural abundance of energy and enthusiasm, which makes you a born entrepreneur. You know how to motivate others and you could sell anything to anyone. You are practical, attentive, pleasure-loving, a risk taker and quick at improvising.

Your strengths

  • You are charming, popular, sensual, enthusiastic and a lover of good times.
  • You are little affected by conflicts or criticism.
  • You are excellent and clear-headed in emergencies.
  • You like spending time with your children.
  • You are very generous.
  • You get along with all personality types, you often keep your friends for life and they appreciate you for your loyalty.

Your points of vigilance

  • You perceive little of what others feel and you express your own emotions little.
  • You can hurt by your language without realizing it.
  • You sometimes manage money well, but sometimes in a very risky way.
  • You live in the present and you plan poorly for the long term.
  • You ignore conflicts instead of resolving them.
  • You do not naturally make lifelong commitments, you get bored easily and you can leave a relationship quickly.

Your career

Your sense of observation makes you an excellent analyst of others’ motivations. Your social skills allow you to use this information to your advantage in your exchanges, which makes you an excellent salesperson. You also react quickly and well to an immediate need, as in an emergency or a crisis. You like new experiences and contact with people, you do not like being locked into a structured framework or into theory, and you want to see an immediate result from your actions. Choose careers rich in interaction and without routine.

The jobs that suit you: sales representative or salesperson, marketing, police officer or detective, nurse or emergency responder, IT technician or network cabler, technical support, entrepreneur, athlete.

You in love

You are enthusiastic and likable, very charming especially at the beginning of a relationship. You are also very generous, sensual, and you live the present moment to the fullest. You do not like making plans for the future, and you can go from one relationship to another to avoid committing. You get bored easily, which brings frequent changes.

You see intimacy as a fun way of enjoying the present moment, from a rather light and physical point of view, more than as an occasion to express your affection.

You are little in tune with what others feel, and you give little recognition and support to your partner. You think actions speak louder than words, and you do not see the need to say what seems obvious to you. Your natural partner is the ISFJ or the ISTJ.

You as a parent

There is a bit of a child in you, and you like playing with your children. You take things as they come and you teach them what seems appropriate to you when situations arise. You believe that many things have no obvious answer, so you are more a friend than an educator. You have no trouble punishing when needed, though. You generally form strong bonds of friendship with your children.

You as a friend

You observe very well and you know how to behave appropriately with all types of people, so you get along with everyone. You have little patience for intuitives, who seem very abstract to you, and you prefer people who have interests close to yours, such as sports. You are very popular because you are enthusiastic, nice, talkative and you know how to have a good time. Many ESTPs keep their friends for life: even while living day to day, you feel loyal to your peers, and your friends appreciate you a lot for your loyalty.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your enthusiasm and your energy serve the Lord: “not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord” (Romans 12:11).
  • Your sense of action makes you available: “Here I am. Send me!” (Isaiah 6:8).
  • Your ability to motivate is a gift: “Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works” (Hebrews 10:24).
  • Your generosity pleases God: “God loves a cheerful giver” (2 Corinthians 9:7).
  • Your loyalty in friendship is biblical: “A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.” (Proverbs 18:24). So is your taste for playing with your children: “The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.”” (Zechariah 8:5).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

Your words hurt without your meaning them to.Proverbs 12:18: the tongue of the wise brings healing. / Proverbs 15:1: a gentle answer turns away wrath. / Ephesians 4:29: good words that build up.Before speaking to someone close to you, check in your head how it will sound. When you have hurt, apologize right away. Learn to say one kind word a day.

Look for novelty within your relationship (outings, projects, trips) instead of changing relationships. Pray for faithfulness every day.
