Each Sunday, note your three priorities for the week. Submit your plans to God before launching out.
You distrust theory and your intuition, and you study little.Proverbs 4:7: get wisdom and understanding. / Proverbs 18:15: the heart of the discerning acquires knowledge. / Proverbs 1:5: the wise hears and increases in learning.Take fifteen minutes a day to study a Bible passage in depth. Use concrete examples to grasp an abstract idea. Ask an intuitive friend to help you see further.
You are more the friend than the educator of your children and you talk little about your feelings.Ephesians 6:4: bring up your children in the Lord. / Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go. / Proverbs 12:25: a kind word makes the heart glad.Tell each child one specific thing you admire in them. Add a time of passing on values to your play: a value, a Bible story. Tell your spouse what seems obvious to you.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say what you feel and keep your word: “let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’” (Matthew 5:37).
  • As a parent, add a time of passing on values to your play (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, your loyalty is a treasure. Resolve disagreements instead of ignoring them (Matthew 18:15).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Start the week by noting your three priorities and handing them to God in prayer.
  • Keep a written budget and give the first share to God.
  • Before speaking in a sensitive conversation, ask yourself how the other will receive your words.
  • Settle one pending conflict, once a week if necessary.
  • Study a Bible passage in depth, a quarter of an hour a day.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me energy, courage and a taste for others. Teach me to weigh my words, to manage what you entrust to me with wisdom and to keep my commitments. Keep me from fleeing when boredom comes. Give me a heart that listens and takes time. May my energy serve your kingdom. Amen.

ESFP.html:
Your portrait

You love people and new experiences. You are lively, fun, and you like being the center of attention. You live here and now. Your relational skills are very strong, which often puts you in the role of peacemaker. You are likable, concerned about the well-being of others, generous and warm.

You are optimistic and you like having fun. You think little about the long-term consequences of your actions. For you, the whole world is a stage and you are constantly putting on a show for others. You would like life to be a continual party where you play the role of host.

You love people and everyone loves you. You are warm and generous with your friends, and you treat just about everyone as one. Once upset, however, you can become very resentful.

Under stress, negative thoughts you are not used to can overwhelm you. You try to explain them with very simple general considerations that do not solve the problem, but at least give you a little relief.

You are practical, but you hate fixed structures and routine. You like to let go, sure of your ability to improvise in any situation. You learn better by practice than from a book. If you have not developed your intuitive side a little, you may avoid situations that call for a lot of theoretical thinking, or that are complex or ambiguous. Hence difficulties at school. On the other hand, you excel when you learn by interacting with others or on the job.

Your sense of aesthetics is highly developed. If you have the means, you will have a beautiful, cleverly arranged home, and you appreciate the fine things in life, such as good food and good wine.

You feel more connected than most types to other people, to children and to animals. You love life and you know how to have fun. You are flexible, adaptable, sincerely interested in people and rather caring. You get a lot of pleasure from life, but you must watch out for its pitfalls.

Your strengths

  • You are enthusiastic, witty, direct and popular: people are drawn to you.
  • You are down-to-earth, practical and flexible.
  • You are artistic and creative.
  • You are generous and warm, and you live the present moment to the fullest.
  • You work well in a team: you do not create problems and you make the environment pleasant.
  • You are sincerely interested in people, and you are appreciated for it.

Your points of vigilance

  • You can be frivolous and manage money in a risky way.
  • You have an extreme aversion to criticism and you take everything personally.
  • You ignore or flee conflicts instead of facing them.
  • You find it hard to commit for the long term, and your taste for novelty can make you change partners often.
  • You do not pay enough attention to your needs, you neglect your health and you may abuse alcohol, food or medication.
  • You speak bluntly, sometimes harshly without meaning to.

Your career

You like working in a team. Not only do you not create fuss, but you make sure the environment is as pleasant as possible. Your ideal careers are those where you use your social skills. Because you like new experiences, choose a job that offers a lot of variety.

The jobs that suit you: artist or actor, sales representative or salesperson, social worker, childcare worker, fashion designer, decorator, consultant, photographer.

You in love

You love love and you try to get the best out of every moment. You take things day by day and you are uncomfortable when you have to think too much about the future or make plans. So you do not like long-term commitments. The trap is going from one relationship to another without ever settling down. You are sensual, generous, warm, and you like making your partner happy.

You handle conflicts poorly. You take any criticism very personally and you see it as an accusation against your whole character. You can react with anger and harsh words that you will regret. You progress by seeing criticism as help, not as an attack. If you learn to hear it without feeling threatened, you will have come a long way toward healthy relationships.

You say things in a blunt and direct way, and you can seem harsh without meaning to. You like people to speak to you in a concrete and factual way. Discussions about the future or the past are not your strong suit: when the subject is not an immediate concern, you lose interest. You mostly want to be happy and bring happiness to others, and you will enliven the couple’s social life. Your natural partner is the ISTJ or the ISFJ.

You as a parent

Your light attitude extends to raising your children. You are warm, affectionate and you take care of them. You like doing things big and enjoying your family. You think too much structure or discipline is not good. If this trait is strong and your spouse does not compensate for it, it can be a problem, because children need a framework throughout their upbringing.

You take care of their daily needs, even though you are casual and your life is full. You prefer to be your children’s friend, but you expect respect and you can, if necessary, take on a more authoritative role. This can confuse some children, who no longer know what to expect. Your children see you as fun, optimistic, affectionate and a bit scattered.

You as a friend

You are enthusiastic and popular, and people are naturally drawn to you. Your genuine interest in others is appreciated. You are very in tune with your five senses and you may be tempted to overload them with too much alcohol, food or medication. You get along with all kinds of people, even though you like spending less time with those you find boring or who communicate at the Intuition or Thinking level. Some disapprove of your pleasure-oriented way of life, and others are put off by your very “straight-talking” way of speaking. You spend most of your time with other extraverted Feeling (F) types, but you have a special place in your heart for people of all types.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your role as peacemaker is blessed: “Blessed are the peacemakers” (Matthew 5:9) and “as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men” (Romans 12:18).
  • Your joy is a strength: “the joy of Yahweh is your strength” (Nehemiah 8:10).
  • Your creativity and your taste for celebration can praise God: “Praise him with tambourine and dancing! Praise him with stringed instruments and flute!” (Psalm 150:4).
  • Your sincere interest in people is biblical: “each of you also to the things of others” (Philippians 2:4).
  • Your generosity and hospitality please God: “Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers” (Hebrews 13:2).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You spend easily and you think little about tomorrow.Proverbs 21:17: whoever loves pleasure will become a poor man. / Luke 12:16-21: the rich man who thought only of the present. / Luke 14:28: count the cost before building.Make a written budget with a share for savings, a share for God and a share for pleasures. Wait 48 hours before any important purchase. Ask a trusted friend to question you about your spending.
You are tempted by excess: alcohol, food, medication.Ephesians 5:18: do not be drunk, but be filled with the Spirit. / 1 Corinthians 6:12, 19-20: be mastered by nothing, the body is the temple of the Spirit. / Proverbs 25:28: a man without self-control is a city broken down, without walls.Set yourself a clear limit before going out. Seek your joy in relationships and service, not only in sensations. If you lose control, ask for help from your church or a professional.
You take criticism as an attack, you react with harsh words or you flee conflict.Proverbs 15:31-32: whoever listens to reproof is wise. / Matthew 18:15: go to the person directly. / Colossians 4:6: speak with grace, seasoned with salt.When you are criticized, breathe and ask: “What is true in this?” Apologize quickly after a harsh word. Soften your frankness: “Here is what I see, and here is why I am telling you.”
You commit with difficulty and you may go from one relationship to another.Matthew 5:37: let your yes be yes. / Proverbs 5:18: rejoice in the wife of your youth. / Hebrews 13:4: let marriage be held in honor.Say yes only if you are ready to keep it. Look for novelty within the same relationship (outings, trips, projects). Pray for faithfulness every day.
Under stress, negative thoughts overwhelm you.Philippians 4:6-8: be anxious for nothing, think about what is true and pure. / 2 Corinthians 10:5: take every thought captive to Christ. / Psalm 42:5: why are you cast down, my soul? Hope in God.Write down each negative thought, then the answer God gives to it. Talk to a close friend instead of distracting yourself. Take a walk and pray.
You are more the friend than the educator of your children, with little framework.Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go. / Ephesians 6:4: bring them up in the Lord. / Hebrews 12:11: discipline yields the fruit of peace.Establish three or four clear rules with your spouse and keep them. Explain the why of each rule. Keep the play and the tenderness, they give weight to your discipline.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, keep your word and stay present when enthusiasm drops (Matthew 5:37).
  • As a parent, add clear structure to your tenderness (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, your warmth is a gift. Also tell the truth gently when a friend is in danger (Galatians 6:1).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Begin the day with a moment of praise, with music if you like, then a passage of the Word.
  • Keep a written budget and regular savings.
  • Ask yourself each evening: “Did I take care of my body today?”
  • When you are criticized, wait ten minutes before answering and pray.
  • Each week do one thing that prepares for the future: a project, savings, an important conversation.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me joy, warmth and the gift of bringing people together. Teach me to think about tomorrow, to guard my body and my mouth, to keep my commitments. Give me a heart that welcomes correction. Fill me with your Spirit so that my joy comes from you. Amen.

ISFP.html:
Your portrait

You live in a world of sensations. You are very in tune with the way things present themselves: taste, sound, touch, smell. You have a strong aesthetic appreciation of art and you are probably an artist in one form or another, because you are gifted at creating and composing what touches the senses. You have a solid value system, which you strive to live out consistently. You need to live according to what you judge right and you rebel against what contradicts it. You choose jobs and careers that let you work freely toward your personal goals based on your values.

You are rather calm, reserved and hard to read. You keep your ideas and opinions for those close to you. You are kind, gentle and sensitive with others, and you want to contribute to their well-being and happiness.

You have a strong affinity for aesthetics and beauty. You love animals and the beauties of nature. You are original, independent, and you need personal space. You appreciate those who take the time to understand you and who support you. Those who know you poorly may see your way of life as lightness, but you take life very seriously. You are constantly collecting information and running it through the sieve of your values, looking for meaning.

You are action-oriented and uncomfortable with concepts and ideas, unless you see a practical application for them. You learn better in a hands-on environment and you get bored easily with traditional, very abstract teaching methods. Your decisions are judged against your subjective beliefs rather than against objective rules or laws.

You are extremely perceptive and aware of others. You constantly gather information about people and look for meaning in it. You are warm and friendly, you truly care about people, you take care of those close to you and you show your love through actions rather than words.

You like neither leading nor controlling others, and you have no wish to be led or controlled. You need space and time for yourself, and you respect that same need in others.

Your values can make you a perfectionist and hard on yourself. You have gifts for artistic creation and for serving others. Life is not so easy for you because you take it seriously, but you have what it takes to make it a rewarding experience, for yourself as well as for others.

Your strengths

  • You are warm, friendly, optimistic, relaxed and attentive.
  • You love aesthetic beauty and you have gifts for artistic creation.
  • You are very perceptive about others, which makes you a precious counselor.
  • You take your commitments seriously and you seek lasting relationships.
  • You respect others’ personal space.
  • You show your affection through actions.

Your points of vigilance

  • You hold back your thoughts and feelings, you say them slowly or not at all in words, and you can feel overshadowed or neglected.
  • You have an extreme aversion to conflict and criticism, which you experience as a personal threat.
  • You can become too cynical and bitter.
  • You plan your financial future poorly, and your life in the present can make you seem slow or lazy.
  • You need your space and you handle it poorly when it is invaded.
  • You are a perfectionist and you judge yourself harshly.

Your career

You are particular. Having a job like everyone else and following a well-trodden path is not for you. Your activity must be consistent with your values. You prefer to live in the present moment, and the bustling environment of a company makes you uncomfortable. You need a lot of space and freedom to put your sensory talents to use. If you give free rein to your natural aptitudes, you can become a wonderful artist: there are many artists among ISFPs. Because you perceive people’s feelings and reactions very well and you have solid inner values, you are also a precious counselor.

The jobs that suit you: artist, musician or composer, designer, childcare worker, social worker, teacher, psychologist, veterinarian, forest ranger, pediatrician.

You in love

You are warm, generous and intense. You may seem light, but you take your relationships very seriously. Unlike other SP types, you seek very long-term relationships. You keep your feelings and opinions hidden, and you make great efforts to please your partner. You are very faithful, you hate conflict and you need a space of freedom.

Some ISFPs who do not express their needs and feelings find themselves overshadowed, neglected, even trampled by others. Cynical by nature, they may then become bitter and give up on certain relationships.

With the introverted Feeling that dominates your personality, you are particularly vulnerable. You do not always say what you think or feel, especially in conflicts, which you hate more than anything, and where you feel personally threatened. You live love through your senses and you express it little with words, considering that actions speak louder than words. You need positive feedback to feel good. Your natural partner is the ESFJ, or, to a lesser extent, the ENFJ.

You as a parent

You take great pride in your role as a parent, and you have a particular affinity with babies and young children. You are relaxed and you have no particular expectations. You treat your children as persons and you encourage them to find their own role in the family. You like playing with them. You do not provide a very structured environment and you find it hard to punish. Because structure and discipline matter for children’s growth, your spouse, if not an ISFP, will have to compensate. Children need limits to tell right from wrong.

You show your love through actions rather than words, through gifts or outings. You are faithful, devoted and selfless. When the children leave the nest, you use your free time to do things for yourself.

You as a friend

You get along with most types, even though you may stay reserved with those you know poorly. You like spending time with those who share your interests and who understand you. You are very attached to your space and your autonomy. You have little patience for those who judge you for your differences. At work, you get along with almost everyone, unless someone encroaches too much on your personal space: sparks may then fly.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your sense of beauty comes from God, who looked at everything he had made: “behold, it was very good” (Genesis 1:31).
  • Your love of nature and animals is biblical: “A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.” (Proverbs 12:10).
  • Your solid values resemble those of Daniel, who “purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself” (Daniel 1:8).
  • Your perceptiveness makes you able to comfort: “Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.” (Proverbs 12:25).
  • Your love through actions has a basis: “My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.” (1 John 3:18).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You keep your feelings in, you feel neglected and you become bitter or cynical.Hebrews 12:15: see that no root of bitterness springs up. / Ephesians 4:31-32: put away bitterness and forgive. / Proverbs 27:5: open rebuke is better than hidden love.Tell God each day what you feel, then tell a trusted person. When you feel neglected, say it simply: “I need you to…” Forgive quickly so as not to hold on to bitterness.
You flee conflict and experience criticism as a threat.Matthew 18:15: go to the person directly. / Ephesians 4:15: speak the truth in love. / Proverbs 12:1: whoever loves correction loves knowledge.Address a small disagreement before it grows. Separate the criticism from your worth. Ask: “What can I learn from this?”
You are a perfectionist and you judge yourself harshly.Romans 8:1: no condemnation in Christ. / 1 John 3:20: God is greater than our heart. / Psalm 103:14: he knows how we are made.Replace the voice that judges you with what God says about you. Finish your projects when they are good enough. Celebrate what you have done each evening.
You decide from your subjective beliefs rather than from objective rules.Proverbs 3:5-6: do not lean on your own understanding. / Romans 12:2: be transformed by the renewing of your mind. / Psalm 119:105: the Word is a lamp to my feet.Pass your values through the sieve of Scripture. Ask yourself: “Is this what the Word says, or what I feel?” Talk about your important decisions with a brother or sister mature in the faith.
You live in the present, you plan the future poorly and you may seem slow.Proverbs 6:6-8: observe the ant and its foresight. / Luke 14:28: count the cost before building. / Colossians 3:23: do everything heartily, as for the Lord.Keep a budget and savings. Note three things to do for the week. Set deadlines for your creative projects.
You find it hard to punish and to set a framework for your children.Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go. / Hebrews 12:11: discipline yields the fruit of peace. / Ephesians 6:4: bring them up in the Lord.Set a few clear rules with your spouse. State them calmly, without over-justifying them. Explain that these limits come from your love.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say your love with words as with actions: “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.” (Proverbs 25:11).
  • As a parent, keep your tenderness and set clear limits (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, stay faithful to your values and patient with those who do not understand you (Colossians 3:13).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Take a time of silence with God in nature or with music, then read a passage of the Word.
  • Express aloud, each day, a feeling or a need to someone close.
  • Make your art a service: offer a work, a song or an object to someone.
  • Write a small financial plan and one thing to move forward each week.
  • Choose a friend or counselor with whom you can speak frankly, including about conflicts.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me a sense of beauty, gentleness and an attentive eye on others. Teach me to say what I feel before bitterness sets in. Deliver me from the fear of conflict and from perfectionism. Help me anchor my values in your Word and set a clear framework for those I love. May my gifts glorify you. Amen.

ENTJ.html:
Your portrait

You were born to lead. You see all kinds of challenges to take on and you want to be the one in charge. You quickly grasp complexities, you absorb a lot of information and you decide fast. You are very career-oriented and you fit naturally into the business world. You constantly scan your environment for problems you can turn into solutions, with a long-term perspective. You often succeed in business because you like to lead, and you are tireless in your efforts.

There is little room for error in your world. You do not like seeing mistakes repeated and you have no patience with inefficiency. You can become very severe, because you are not naturally attuned to feelings and you do not believe you must adapt your decisions to them. You have little patience with those who do not see things as you do. You are energetic, intimidating and domineering.

You decide fast and you are quick to state your opinions and decisions. Some ENTJs decide too fast, without understanding all the stakes or all the possible solutions. Others find it hard to apply logic to their ideas: they have brilliant ideas, but struggle to know how to act. You can become dictatorial, giving orders without good reason and without regard for the people concerned.

Even though you are not naturally attuned to the feelings of others, you often have strong emotional surges. They are powerful, and you keep them to yourself because you see them as a weakness. This can become a serious problem.

You like people, and nothing pleases you as much as a lively and difficult conversation. You respect above all those who resist you and defend their point of view convincingly. Few people do, because you have enormous self-confidence and excellent verbal skills. Even the most self-assured can doubt in a debate with you.

At home, you are in charge as at work. Because your career takes up so much of you, you can be constantly absent from home, physically or mentally.

You have a lot of power: you are authoritative, innovative, a long-term thinker, very gifted at translating theories and possibilities into solid action plans, and extremely energetic.

Your strengths

  • You are sincerely interested in people’s ideas and thoughts.
  • You are enthusiastic, energetic, straightforward and direct.
  • You take your commitments very seriously, and you have high standards and expectations.
  • You are impartial and very gifted with money.
  • You encourage knowledge and training in all areas of life.
  • You know how to turn a conflict into a positive lesson and you accept constructive criticism well.
  • You know how to punish when necessary and to turn the page when a relationship is over.

Your points of vigilance

  • You quickly enter confrontation and conversations where one wins and the other loses.
  • You find it hard to listen and you criticize opinions and attitudes that do not resemble yours.
  • You poorly perceive people’s feelings, you find it hard to express your love and to give compliments.
  • You want to be in charge of everything, you give orders, you can become dictatorial and intimidating.
  • You are very hard and intolerant of disorder and inefficiency.
  • You make hasty decisions.
  • Under extreme stress, you can explode in anger.

Your career

You are particularly well suited to lead. You know how to clearly identify problems and innovative solutions for the good of an organization in the short and long term. With your strong desire to lead, you are uncomfortable in a subordinate position.

The jobs that suit you: business management, entrepreneur, IT consultant, lawyer, judge, university professor.

You in love

You take your commitments very seriously. As in the rest of your life, you want to be the leader and the one in charge of the relationship. You often redefine the “rules” of the couple, although your commitment remains constant. If the relationship no longer offers any opportunity to learn, you end it without looking back.

You are generally successful in your career and with money, which shields you from financial conflicts in the couple. On the other hand, because you work a lot, this creates other problems. You want to be in charge of the relationship to the point of stifling your partner and even tiring yourself. In intimacy, you are imaginative and enthusiastic, and your instinct to lead carries your partner along.

You generally have no problem with self-confidence and you are not emotionally dependent. You enjoy being loved, but you do not need to hear it as often as most types. Without a conscious effort, you do not say to your partner the intimate words they need.

You see conflict as an opportunity to learn. This can be a problem in intimacy: Feeling-type partners hate conflict and criticism and avoid them. Your tendency to confrontation can threaten them greatly. To remedy this, develop your Feeling side or choose a Thinking-type partner.

You have a lot to offer: you are devoted, enthusiastic and ready to make great efforts. Your relationship will be based on mutual respect and constant development. Your natural partner is the INTP, or, to a lesser extent, the ISTP.

You as a parent

You take your role as a parent very seriously and you consider it your responsibility to make sure your child keeps progressing. You are strict, with very high expectations, and you pass on your love of knowledge. You expect your children to follow your example and honor you by respecting the house rules. There is little room for error and you become authoritarian when rules are broken. Your children generally have a lot of respect for you and become responsible and independent adults.

Your children tend to rebel in adolescence, and this is particularly true with an ENTJ parent. Once grown, they no longer want to be controlled, and it is hard for you to let go. You can be aggressive, dictatorial and give arbitrary orders. In the long run, this creates an oppressive environment for the child.

You as a friend

You are sociable, intelligent, energetic and interested in the ideas of others. You like conversations with people who share your views or who have something new to teach you, and you savor lively intellectual exchanges. You are direct, which sometimes puts people on the defensive. Those who are uncomfortable with confrontation or less self-assured may fall silent, which is a pity, because many have precious things to offer. You look for people who have opinions and interests close to yours, and you have little patience with those who are very different. You are drawn to people of power, whom you admire even when you disagree with them. Your closest friendships are with other intuitives, especially extraverts: ENTJ, ENTP, ENFJ and ENFP.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your gift for leading is biblical: “he who rules, with diligence” (Romans 12:8). Nehemiah gives you the model: “Come, let’s build up the wall of Jerusalem” (Nehemiah 2:17).
  • Your long-term vision serves a people: “Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint” (Proverbs 29:18).
  • Your energy can be for God: “Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.” (Ecclesiastes 9:10).
  • Your taste for learning is blessed: “that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel” (Proverbs 1:5).
  • Your lively debates can build up: “Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.” (Proverbs 27:17).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You dominate, you give orders and you want to control everything.Luke 22:25-26: among you, the one who leads must be like the one who serves. / Mark 10:42-45: the Son of Man came to serve. / 1 Peter 5:3: lead without lording it over others, as an example.For each decision, ask yourself: “Whom am I serving?” Truly delegate: entrust the task and the power. Publicly thank those who helped you.
You have great self-confidence and you decide too fast.Proverbs 3:5-7: do not be wise in your own eyes. / Proverbs 19:2: one who hurries his steps misses his way. / Proverbs 15:22: plans succeed with many counselors.For every important decision, wait 24 hours and seek advice from two people who think differently from you. Listen to their objections to the end before answering.
You are hard, intimidating and give few compliments.Proverbs 12:18: the tongue of the wise brings healing. / Colossians 3:21: do not discourage. / 1 Thessalonians 5:11: encourage one another.For every criticism, first give a precise and sincere compliment. Each day tell someone what they did well. Ask: “How did you take what I said?”
You hide your emotions as a weakness and you explode under stress.2 Corinthians 12:9-10: God’s power is made perfect in weakness. / Proverbs 16:32: one who rules his spirit is better than one who takes a city. / Psalm 62:8: pour out your heart before God.Name your emotions to God aloud. Choose a confidant to whom you can say what you feel. Recognize your fatigue before the explosion and take rest.
You are absent from your family because of your work.Psalm 127:1-2: it is vain to rise early if God does not build the house. / Matthew 16:26: what does it profit to gain the world and lose your soul? / Mark 6:31: come apart and rest.Block family evenings in your calendar and respect them like your business appointments. Take one day of rest a week. Put your phone down during meals.
You demand a lot of your children and you find it hard to let go.Ephesians 6:4: do not provoke your children. / Colossians 3:21: so that they won’t be discouraged. / Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go.Replace one order with a question each day. Explain your rules. In adolescence, gradually move from control to accompaniment.
You do not listen to opinions that contradict you and you criticize what is different.Proverbs 12:15: the wise listens to counsel. / James 1:19: quick to listen, slow to speak. / Philippians 2:3-4: regard others as better than yourself.Restate what the other has just said before answering. Look for what is right in their point of view. Spend time with people very different from you.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, learn to say the words of love: “Husbands, love your wives, and don’t be bitter against them.” (Colossians 3:19). Give the other a place to decide.
  • As a parent, be demanding and tender: “Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.” (Colossians 3:21).
  • As a friend, listen as much as you speak, and let the shy finish their sentences (James 1:19).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Begin each day with prayer and the Word, before the agenda: “Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.” (Proverbs 16:3).
  • Each day, listen to one person for three minutes without interrupting.
  • Each day, give someone a precise compliment.
  • Take one day of rest a week and keep evenings for your family.
  • Before any important decision, wait 24 hours and ask the opinion of two counselors.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me vision, strength and a taste for leading. Teach me to serve rather than to dominate, to listen before deciding and to say the words that encourage. Keep me from anger and pride. Bring my heart back to my family. May everything I build serve your glory. Amen.

INTJ.html:
Your portrait

You live in a world of ideas and strategic planning. You value intelligence, knowledge and competence. You have high standards that you constantly strive to meet, and to a lesser extent you expect the same from others.

You focus your energy on observing the world and you generate ideas and opportunities. Your mind constantly gathers and connects information, and you quickly grasp new ideas. Your main interest is not understanding a concept, but applying it in a useful way. Unlike the INTP, you do not follow an idea as far as possible: you like to draw conclusions from it and put them into action, which meets your need to organize.

Your systemic approach and your intuition make you an excellent scientist, who puts his ideas into a form useful to others. You find it hard to express your inner images, ideas and abstractions: they are very personal and hard to translate. You are nevertheless trained to convert them into a plan or a system that is easy to explain. Your extreme respect for knowledge pushes you to explain them to those who deserve it.

You are a natural leader, but you often stay in the background until you see a real need to take the lead. Once in a leadership position, you are very effective: you see objectively the reality of a situation and you know how to change what does not work. You are the supreme strategist: you constantly confront the available ideas with your current strategy to foresee every eventuality.

You spend a lot of time in your ideas and you take little interest in the thoughts or feelings of others. You are quick to judge. Your intuitions are often very advanced and you are convinced you are right. If you do not complete your understanding with a clear expression of your views, you are often misunderstood, and you then tend to put it down to the other’s limits rather than to your difficulty in expressing yourself. This can push you to reject others too quickly and to become arrogant and elitist.

You are ambitious and a long-term thinker. Many INTJs become engineers or researchers. Others find challenges in business, where organizing and planning are needed. You do not like disorder, inefficiency, or what is confused or unclear, and you put enormous energy into consolidating your information into structured models.

Others find you reserved, because you are not very demonstrative and not inclined to praise or positive support. This does not mean you have no affection or regard, but you do not feel the need to express it. You are sometimes thought rigid and set in your ways. That is false: you are always looking for the best strategy and you are generally open to another way of doing things.

Your intuition is turned inward. You are more interested in what could be than in what is, and you like peace and silence for your inner journeys. You are not comfortable at social events, and the bigger the group, the clumsier you are. You thrive with one person in front of you. Time matters enormously to you: you prefer a simple life that leaves you time for your interests to a big house that forces you to work for others.

Under stress, you can absorb yourself in details you would normally ignore, or indulge in repetitive sensory activities, such as drinking too much. Your Achilles’ heel is extraverted Sensing: repressed, it can claim its due by roundabout ways, in the form of obsessions, compulsions or deprivations (food, alcohol, sex or other).

You have an enormous capacity to accomplish great things. You are almost always very competent. If you practice tolerance and strive to communicate your ideas clearly, you have everything in hand to lead a rich and rewarding life.

Your strengths

  • You are not disturbed by conflict or criticism, and you are confident.
  • You are intelligent and capable.
  • You take your relationships and commitments seriously and you seek to improve them.
  • You know how to listen.
  • You know how to end a relationship that is going badly.
  • You are a strategist and an effective leader when the need arises.

Your points of vigilance

  • You are not always in tune with the feelings of others, and you respond to conflict with logic rather than emotional support.
  • You find it hard to express your feelings.
  • You easily believe you are always right and you accept criticism poorly.
  • You can become arrogant, curt and isolate yourself.
  • Your constant quest for improvement can call your relationships into question.
  • You think more than you act, and you find it hard to reconcile reality with your inner visions.
  • Under stress, you can fall into excesses (alcohol, food, obsessions).

Your career

More than any other type, you shine at grasping complex theories, applying them to problems and developing long-term strategies. You are happy and effective in careers where you have a lot of autonomy.

The jobs that suit you: scientist, engineer, professor or teacher, doctor or dentist, business and organizational strategist, administrator or manager, military leader, lawyer, judge, programmer or systems analyst.

You in love

You constantly try to improve the quality of your life and your relationships. You take your commitments seriously but you remain open to change if you see a possible improvement. You can sometimes be insensitive to others’ emotional needs. You nevertheless strive to do your best and to progress.

Sometimes, what you see and understand intuitively is purer and more perfect than the reality of a relationship. You find it hard to reconcile reality with your imagination. You are not especially in tune with your feelings or those of others, and you easily believe you are right. Your self-confidence is attractive, but your lack of sensitivity can be a problem. Be more attentive to the effect of your words. In case of conflict, pay attention to your spouse’s emotional needs instead of treating the conflict as an interesting idea to analyze.

You seek to perfect your intimacy, in creativity and intensity. You approach it in a more cerebral way than as an occasion to express your love. Those who have grasped the importance of these signs of affection are much more tender.

Your greatest relational flaw is thinking about things rather than doing them, and struggling to reconcile reality with your visions. You nevertheless have every chance of living healthy relationships, because you do not hesitate to end those that do not work. Your natural partner is the ENFP or the ENTP.

You as a parent

Your main goal is to raise intelligent, self-reliant and independent children. You want them to think for themselves and make their own decisions, so you leave them room to grow.

You show little support or love. Because your own need for affection is low, you find it hard to sense that of your children, which can create a distance. To remedy this, consciously take care of others’ emotional needs.

You as a friend

You are hard to know and hard to approach. You are serious, but you also know how to let go and have fun, with a touch of sarcasm. You especially like spending time with other intuitive thinkers who like to speculate about ideas. Many INTJs believe they are always right, and some find it hard to accept what they perceive as superiority or snobbery. It is not snobbery: it is a perception of those with a strong Feeling preference. Others simply have no interest in your theoretical activities.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your strategy is biblical: “Plans are established by advice; by wise guidance you wage war!” (Proverbs 20:18). Jesus himself speaks of counting the cost before building (Luke 14:28-31).
  • Your intelligence is a gift from God: “Now as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.” (Daniel 1:17).
  • Your restraint has its value: “He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.” (Proverbs 17:27).
  • Your taste for wisdom can be fulfilled: “But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.” (James 1:5).
  • Your discreet leadership joins that of the servant: “But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.” (Luke 22:26).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

Replace the excess with walking, sport or prayer. Talk to a trusted person if you lose control.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say your feelings and handle conflicts by listening first (Ephesians 4:32).
  • As a parent, add tenderness to autonomy: “Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.” (Colossians 3:21), and tell them you love them.
  • As a friend, drop the superiority and let yourself be known (Philippians 2:3).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Take a time of silence and the Word each day. Your taste for calm is an asset here (Psalm 46:10).
  • Each day, say one thing you feel aloud to someone.
  • After every important exchange, ask: “How did you take what I said?”
  • Turn one idea into concrete action each week.
  • Take care of your sleep and limit alcohol, especially when you are stressed.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me intelligence, vision and a taste for strategy. Keep me from pride and open my heart to others. Teach me to express myself clearly, to listen with compassion and to accept criticism. Turn my plans into actions that serve you. Amen.

ENTP.html:
Your portrait

Your main interest in life is understanding the world you live in. You constantly absorb ideas and images about the situations that arise, and your intuition lets you size up a situation very quickly and accurately. You understand your environment better than all the other types, apart from your ENFP cousins.

This ability to intuitively understand people and situations gives you a clear advantage. You understand quickly and deeply, you are flexible and you adapt well to a wide range of tasks. By developing your skills and intuitions, you become very ingenious at solving problems.

You see possibilities everywhere. You get enthusiastic about your ideas and you know how to spread that enthusiasm, which brings you the support you need to carry out your visions.

Generating possibilities interests you more than building action plans or making decisions. Following through on an idea is often a chore, and for some it becomes a habit never to finish what they have begun. You need to think your ideas through fully.

Even though you prefer absorbing information to deciding, you are entirely rational and logical in drawing conclusions. When you apply Thinking to your intuitive perceptions, the result can be very powerful. You can be extremely visionary, inventive and enterprising.

You are talkative, quick-witted, and you like to dialogue. You like to debate and you can even switch sides, sometimes just for the love of debate.

You are sometimes called the “lawyer” type. Your actions and decisions are based on rules or laws. If you defend someone who has committed a crime, you can exploit the loopholes of the law to help him, and if you win, you judge your action right because it is legal. The client’s guilt or innocence matters little to you. That is why others may find you dishonest.

Sensing and Feeling are your weak points. You can neglect details or become too hard and aggressive. Under stress, you become obsessed with minor details that seem very important to you at the moment.

In general, you are an optimistic visionary. You like challenges and difficulties. Faced with a problem, you improvise and quickly find a creative solution. Creative, intelligent, curious and theoretical, you have a wide range of possibilities before you.

Your strengths

  • You are enthusiastic, optimistic, popular and sometimes very charming.
  • You have excellent communication skills.
  • You are very interested in developing your relationships.
  • You are flexible, approachable and full of ideas, always ready to launch into a big project.
  • You know how to make money.
  • You take your commitments and relationships very seriously, and you bounce back after a relationship ends.

Your points of vigilance

  • You tend not to follow through on your plans and ideas.
  • Your love of debate can go as far as provocation and one-upmanship.
  • You take risks with money and you spend it more than you manage it.
  • You may change partners often or abandon a relationship that no longer offers possibilities for development.
  • You sometimes neglect your loved ones when you are caught up in a new project.
  • You ignore what others feel and you can become hard or aggressive.

Your career

You can succeed in many careers. You need a profession that gives you great personal freedom and where you can use your creativity to generate ideas and solve problems. You are not fully happy in a subordinate position.

The jobs that suit you: lawyer, psychologist, entrepreneur, photographer, consultant, engineer, scientist, actor, sales representative or salesperson, marketing, computer programmer or systems analyst.

You in love

You are generally in a good mood, optimistic and relaxed. You find great pleasure in exchanging, especially in debating theories and concepts that interest you. You can start arguments because you like debate. You are playful, sociable and sometimes very charming. Your problem is neglecting your close relationships when you are caught up in a new idea or a new plan.

You constantly wonder how to improve the relationship and you enthusiastically embrace new ideas and new projects for you and your partner. Your tendency not to follow through can frustrate your partner, and your risk-taking can drag the family into an uncomfortable financial situation.

In intimacy, you are enthusiastic, attentive and involved. You like spontaneity rather than fixed schedules. You approach it as a physical act more than as an occasion to express your affection. Beware of your tendency to ignore what others feel. Your natural partner is the INFJ or the INTJ.

You as a parent

There is a child in you. You approach parenthood by having fun, with a serious goal: to help your child think logically and independently. You are sometimes contradictory. One moment you are very interested in your children, then you neglect them without meaning to as soon as a big project comes along.

You as a friend

You get along with almost all types of people. You are flexible and easygoing, and you truly like exchanging with others. You surround yourself with intelligent, capable people full of ideas, and you love debating with someone who can stand up to you. Sometimes you fall into one-upmanship, which can weaken certain relationships.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your eloquence can serve the Word, like that of Apollos, “an eloquent man… mighty in the Scriptures” (Acts 18:24). Paul also “reasoned with them from the Scriptures” (Acts 17:2).
  • Your contagious enthusiasm is a gift: “not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord” (Romans 12:11).
  • Your flexibility serves the gospel: “I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some” (1 Corinthians 9:22).
  • Your ability to encourage goes far: “Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works” (Hebrews 10:24).
  • Your optimism can be anchored in God: “Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.” (Romans 15:13).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

Keep your word, even when enthusiasm drops. Invent novelty in your relationship rather than leaving it.

Take a break or a walk.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, bring consistency: “let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’” (Matthew 5:37), and say your love through regular actions.
  • As a parent, be present even when a project attracts you: “you shall teach them diligently to your children” (Deuteronomy 6:7).
  • As a friend, your debating spirit can sharpen others without wounding them (Proverbs 27:17).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Begin the day with the Word and prayer, then choose one single priority to finish.
  • Finish one project before starting another, and note each time what you have completed.
  • Before a debate, decide your goal: understanding, building up or winning. Choose the first two.
  • Keep a written budget and give God the first share.
  • Keep a project-free time each week with your family.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me curiosity, speech and a taste for ideas. Teach me to finish what I begin and to stay faithful to my commitments. Keep me from provocation and from reasoning that sidesteps justice. Give me a heart attentive to my family and to those around me. May my ideas serve your kingdom. Amen.

INTP.html:
Your portrait

You see everything in terms of possibilities for improvement or transformation. You live mostly in your own mind, with the ability to analyze difficult problems, identify patterns and find logical explanations. You are driven to turn problems into logical explanations, and you give less value to the outside world. This can become a sense of personal responsibility: solving theoretical problems and helping society progress toward greater understanding.

Your mind constantly generates new theories or proves or disproves existing ones. You approach problems with enthusiasm and skepticism, without concern for established rules and opinions, defining your own approach. You look for patterns and logical explanations for everything that interests you. You like new ideas, abstractions and theories, and you like discussing them with others. You can seem dreamy and distant because you spend a lot of time in your head. You hate routine. You prefer to build complex theoretical solutions and leave implementation to others. You invest enormous time and energy in solving a problem.

You do not like leading or controlling people. You are very tolerant and flexible in most situations, unless one of your deep convictions is violated or challenged: you can then take a very rigid position. You are very shy with new people, but very confident and sociable with those you know well or during discussions on theories you master perfectly.

You do not respect decisions made on a subjective or sentimental basis. You always look for a logical conclusion, and you do not understand the importance of emotional considerations in a decision. You are therefore rarely in tune with what people feel and little inclined to respond to their emotional needs.

You find it hard to give the warmth and support that relationships sometimes need. You can become too critical and ironic. If you cannot use your abilities, you can become negative and cynical. You can also be absent-minded and disconnected from reality, forgetting to pay your bills or dressing without taste.

It is important to you that ideas and facts be expressed correctly and succinctly. Sometimes your understanding of an idea is not easy for others to grasp, and you do not try to adapt it to make it understandable. Yet an amazing discovery is worth nothing if you are the only person who understands it.

You are very independent, unconventional and original. You give little value to popularity and security. You are a complex character, sometimes restless and capricious, with unconventional thought patterns that help you analyze ideas differently. Many scientific breakthroughs come from people like you.

You are in your element when you can work on theories independently. In an environment that values your creative genius and your eccentricity, you can accomplish truly remarkable things. You are a pioneer of new ideas.

Your strengths

  • You love your loved ones with a love almost childlike in its purity.
  • You are generally relaxed and easygoing, with simple needs and few demands.
  • You are rich in imagination and creativity.
  • You are not personally threatened by conflict or criticism.
  • You are faithful and loyal once committed, and your love is honest and uncomplicated.

Your points of vigilance

  • You are little in tune with the feelings of others, little inclined to respond to their emotional needs, and you find it hard to express your own.
  • You distrust others, you remain hard to reach and your circle of relationships is small.
  • You are not very gifted with practical matters.
  • You ignore conflicts or you get angry, and you approach them analytically when your partner mainly wants to be supported.
  • You can become too critical, ironic, cynical or negative.
  • You can take a very rigid position when one of your beliefs is challenged.

Your career

You have a particular gift for producing and analyzing theories. You are perceptive and creative, which lets you quickly grasp complex abstract thoughts. You are happy in careers that leave you great autonomy and where you can work alone on developing and analyzing complex theories. The goal of your work is the discovery of a truth rather than a practical application.

The jobs that suit you: scientist (especially physics or chemistry), strategic planner, mathematician, university professor, programmer or systems analyst, technical writer, engineer, lawyer, judge, forensic researcher.

You in love

Your inner world is rich in imagination and excitement, and the outside world often seems flat to you. This can leave you lacking motivation to form and maintain relationships. So you do not have a very large circle of important relationships. You prefer a few very close bonds, which you value greatly. You are hard to reach until the other has shown themselves worthy of hearing your thoughts. Once committed, you are very faithful and loyal, and your bonds are affectionate, pure and simple.

You approach your intimate relationships very seriously. You are generally faithful, loyal, easygoing, with simple daily needs. Your inner life is theoretical and complex, but your outer life is rather simple: you limit the complexity of the outside world to concentrate on your theories. In intimacy, you approach things with enthusiasm and you use your imagination to enjoy it to the fullest.

Your biggest concern in the couple is your slowness in understanding and meeting your partner’s emotional needs. You can be extremely devoted and deeply in love, and yet not understand your partner and not express your feelings.

You do not like conflicts and you ignore them when they arrive. You can also approach them analytically, which makes the situation worse if your partner simply wants to feel supported and loved. Most people, especially Feeling types, mainly want to be encouraged and supported when they are angry. Your natural partner is the ENTJ, or, to a lesser extent, the ESTJ.

You as a parent

Your greatest goal is to see your children become independent and rational adults. You encourage them to grow as individuals rather than forcing them into a mold. You emphasize autonomy through education and you respect their opinions and wishes.

You are relaxed and flexible, and you count on your spouse to give the necessary framework. Because you do not live in a very structured way yourself, you do not want to create that kind of environment. If your spouse is not a Judging (J) type, your children may lack limits. Despite this unstructured approach, you take your role very seriously and you make great efforts so that they become wise and independent adults. Your children see you as faithful, fair, tolerant and attentive.

You as a friend

You have friends who share your interests and activities. Because you like theories, ideas and concepts, you have little patience and understanding for people with a Sensing preference.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your intellectual curiosity is honorable: “the glory of kings is to search out a matter” (Proverbs 25:2).
  • Your quest for truth finds its center in Christ: “in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden” (Colossians 2:3).
  • Your simple and pure love resembles the one Jesus praises: “unless you turn, and become as little children” (Matthew 18:3).
  • Your loyalty is precious: “A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17).
  • Your originality can serve God: “Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed” (Romans 12:2).

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say your love with words and listen before analyzing (Ephesians 4:32).
  • As a parent, add limits to your trust and say your affection aloud (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, open up to a small circle and stay faithful (Proverbs 17:17).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Meditate each day on a passage of the Word: “his delight is in Yahweh’s law” (Psalm 1:2).
  • Each day say a word of affection to someone and ask a question about their needs.
  • Explain an idea in three simple sentences to a non-specialist.
  • Reserve one slot a week for practical tasks (bills, tidying).
  • Keep regular contact with two or three close friends.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me a mind that searches, analyzes and understands. Keep me from coldness and irony. Teach me to listen with compassion, to express what I feel and to make my ideas accessible. Help me in practical matters and in my family. May my search for truth always lead me to you. Amen.

ENFJ.html:
Your portrait

You are people-focused. More than any other type, you have excellent relational skills. You have a particular talent for bringing out the best in others, and your main interest is to give love and support. You have the ability to get from others the reactions you are looking for. Your motives are generally selfless, but some ENFJs may use this power to manipulate.

You are hard on yourself and you have dark thoughts when you are alone. Some then try to fill their lives with activities with other people. You set your priorities according to others’ needs, to the point of forgetting your own.

You are more reserved than the other extraverted types. Even if your convictions are strong, you may not express them if they risk hurting someone. Faced with a conflict, you may place the other’s needs before your own.

You can feel very lonely even when you are well surrounded. This loneliness can be aggravated by your tendency not to show your true nature.

People love you. You are fun, honest, brilliant, energetic and you give off a lot of self-confidence. You like working with people, and your incredible ability to understand them makes you an ideal counselor. You like being the center of attention and you are very gifted at teaching. You like purely logical reasoning less.

You have a special gift with people and you truly enjoy being of service. You have a very strong need for close and intimate relationships. Once committed, you are very faithful and trustworthy.

If you have not found your place in the world, you can be very sensitive to criticism, worry excessively or feel guilty. You can also become very manipulative.

In general, you are charming, warm, likable and creative. You have the particular ability to see the potential for development in others and to help them progress.

Your strengths

  • You communicate well orally and you are perceptive about people’s thoughts and motivations.
  • You motivate, you inspire and you bring out the best in others.
  • You are affectionate, fun, energetic and optimistic, with a good sense of humor.
  • You have financial skills.
  • You are loyal and devoted, and you seek lasting relationships.
  • You look for situations where everyone wins, and you like meeting the needs of others.

Your points of vigilance

  • You can be smothering and overprotective.
  • You tend to control or manipulate.
  • You do not pay enough attention to your own needs.
  • You criticize opinions and attitudes that do not resemble yours.
  • You are extremely sensitive to conflicts and you try to avoid them, even if it means accepting what goes against your values.
  • You blame yourself when things go wrong and you do not give yourself credit when they go well.

Your career

You have a lot of room to maneuver in choosing a job. The important thing is that you work with people and that you have enough challenges to stimulate your creativity.

The jobs that suit you: consultant, psychologist, social worker, teacher, representative, human resources, director, politician or diplomat, writer.

You in love

You are totally dedicated to your partner and to the relationship, and you take your commitments seriously. If a relationship fails, you first feel guilty, then you move on without looking back. You have a habit of checking in a lot on your partner, which can become smothering.

In intimacy, you see an opportunity to express your love and you seek your partner’s happiness and satisfaction. You can fall into routine. Even if you do not ask for it, you need to receive sweet words. Because a large part of your satisfaction comes from the happiness of others, you can ignore your own needs.

You hate conflicts. You prefer to ignore them or even hide them rather than attack them head-on. You may accept something that goes against your values only to end an uncomfortable situation, and the problem returns later. Remember that the world does not stop because there is a disagreement, and that ignoring a problem does not make it disappear. Your natural partner is the INFP, or, to a lesser extent, the ISFP.

You as a parent

You take your role as a parent very seriously. Passing on values and goals to your children is paramount for you. You are fairly strict, with high expectations of their behavior, but also warm and affectionate. You have well-defined ideas about what is right and wrong and you tend to watch over them closely.

It is not always easy to be the child of an ENFJ, because your behavior can be smothering. At puberty, your children need more space and feel your protective side as suffocating. This gets worse if you have manipulative tendencies: as they grow up, they see them and begin to question your values. Yet you have only good intentions for them, and they see you as warm, although strict.

You as a friend

You are warm, sociable, supportive, generous and in tune with the feelings and points of view of others. You are energetic and fun. You seek authenticity and you are very sensitive to the needs of others. You are interested in all personality types, but you like spending less time with those with a Sensing preference, whose “live in the moment” attitude can clash with your value system. You are uncomfortable with objective judgments that do not take people into account, so you have few close friendships with Thinking types. You get along fully with xNFxs and xSxJs.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your gift of encouragement is biblical: Barnabas was called “Son of Encouragement” (Acts 4:36), and “he who exhorts, to his exhorting” (Romans 12:8).
  • Your talent for teaching and inspiring is a service: “he who teaches, to his teaching” (Romans 12:7).
  • Your ability to bring out the best in others is a work of building up: “Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.” (1 Thessalonians 5:11).
  • Your perceptiveness can be guided by God: “Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.” (Proverbs 20:5).
  • Your loyalty joins that of the true friend: “A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17).

Explain your values instead of imposing them. Tell them what you admire in them every day.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, say what you need and let your partner breathe (Galatians 6:5).
  • As a parent, keep your tender demands and leave space: “Fathers, don’t provoke your children, so that they won’t be discouraged.” (Colossians 3:21).
  • As a friend, let yourself be truly known and agree to be helped (Galatians 6:2).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Every day, take ten minutes alone with God before any activity with others.
  • Tell one person one thing you need each week.
  • Express a disagreement gently instead of avoiding it, as soon as it comes up.
  • Write down each evening three things that went well, including one you did yourself.
  • Share your heart with a trusted friend, without hiding behind the role of the one who helps.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me a heart that loves and encourages. Teach me to take care of myself too, to tell the truth gently and not to manipulate. Keep me from guilt and loneliness. Give me the freedom to let others grow. May my love resemble yours. Amen.

INFJ.html:
Your portrait

You are gentle, caring, complex and intuitive. Artistic and creative, you live in a world of meanings and hidden possibilities. Your type is one of the rarest.

You like things to be well ordered. You constantly look for the best system and you redefine your priorities accordingly. You know things intuitively, without being able to say why, and without in-depth knowledge of the subject. You have enormous faith in your instincts and your intuitions. There is something like a conflict between your inner world and the outer world, which means you are not as organized as the other Judging-preference types. There is a semblance of disorder in you within an otherwise ordered tendency.

You have a strange vision of people and situations. You have “feelings” about things and you understand them intuitively. Some INFJs report having had strong premonitions, for example about a problem with a loved one, before discovering later that there had been an accident. Other types often laugh at these intuitions, and even you find it hard to explain them. So you keep them to yourself and rarely share them. You are deep, complex, reserved and hard to understand.

You are also authentic and warm. You hold a special place in the hearts of those close to you who see your gifts. You care about people’s feelings and you are very sensitive to conflicts. You tend to internalize them in your body and become very restless.

You trust your own instincts above all, hence a tendency to ignore the opinion of others: you believe you are right. You are also a perfectionist and rarely at peace with yourself. There is always something you should do better. You are a disciple of continuous improvement and you do not take time to savor your successes. You have strong values and you need to live according to what you judge good. You are gentle and easygoing in many respects, but you have very high expectations of yourself and your family.

You are a patient, devoted and protective parent, with strong bonds with your children. You have high expectations and you push them to be the best they can be.

At work, you are comfortable where you can be creative and independent. You have a natural affinity for art, but also for the sciences, where your intuition is put to good use, and for the service professions. You are less gifted for meticulous and precise tasks.

Your strengths

  • You are warm, sensitive and concerned about the feelings of others, and you know how to listen.
  • You communicate well, especially in writing.
  • You always seek the best possible relationship.
  • You take your commitments very seriously and you seek lasting relationships.
  • You have strong values and intuitions that give you a sense of knowing, which prepares you to lead.
  • You are a patient, devoted parent, ready to make sacrifices for your children.

Your points of vigilance

  • You trust your instincts above all and you easily believe you are right.
  • You are a perfectionist, rarely at peace with yourself, and you do not savor your successes.
  • You have an extreme aversion to conflict and criticism, which you internalize in your body.
  • Your expectations are very high for others and for yourself, and you may go from one relationship to another in search of the perfect partner.
  • You are reserved and you keep your intuitions to yourself.
  • You manage money poorly and you find it hard to leave a bad relationship.

Your career

You need more than a simple job. Everything you do must be in tune with your values and what you believe is right. With your strong values and your intuitive visions, you are better suited to lead than to be a subordinate.

The jobs that suit you: teacher, doctor or dentist, chiropractor or reflexologist, psychologist, psychiatrist, social worker, musician or artist, photographer, childcare worker.

You in love

You are thoughtful and warm. You like showing and receiving love. You are a perfectionist and you constantly seek the perfect relationship. This can frustrate your partner, but it is also the sign of a very sincere commitment. Sometimes, you fall into the habit of going from one relationship to another in search of the ideal partner. You look for long-term relationships, even if you do not always find them.

In intimacy, you experience love as an almost spiritual experience. You seek to bond with your partner’s soul, and it is very important to you that they be happy. You give your love generously, in a concrete way.

You find it hard to leave a bad relationship, and you have an extreme aversion to conflict and criticism. Your natural partner is the ENTP or the ENFP.

You as a parent

You are a warm and caring parent. Your goal is to help your children become adults who know the difference between right and wrong. You see them as people who have a say in family decisions, and you want them to think for themselves and make the right decisions. You can also be very demanding.

You take your role as a parent with great seriousness and you make sacrifices for your children without ulterior motives or regret.

You as a friend

Your family is your priority, but you truly value your friendships. You seek authenticity and depth, and you especially appreciate those who appreciate you for who you are. You can have friends of all types, but you have little patience for those you judge dishonest or corrupt. All kinds of people are drawn to you and you are probably more popular than you think. Your close friends appreciate you for your different way of seeing things and for your ability to inspire and motivate others.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your intuition can be matured: “But solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.” (Hebrews 5:14).
  • Your pen can pass on what God gives you: “Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book” (Jeremiah 30:2).
  • Your compassion is a spiritual garment: “a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility” (Colossians 3:12).
  • Your strong values have an anchor: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them” (Proverbs 11:3).
  • Your devotion to your children has a promise: “children are a heritage of Yahweh” (Psalm 127:3).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word
