Write down what this relationship costs you and what it brings you. Ask God for the wisdom to stay or to leave.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, welcome your partner as they are: “accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you” (Romans 15:7).
  • As a parent, keep your standards and add grace to them (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, share your different way of seeing things: you help others see further (Proverbs 27:17).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Begin each day with a time of silence and the Word, and note what God tells you.
  • Submit every strong intuition to a trusted brother or sister before acting.
  • Each evening, write down what was done well before thinking about what is missing.
  • Say what bothers you in writing or aloud, within 24 hours.
  • Take one small step a week for money and practical tasks.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me sensitivity, intuition and a taste for meaning. Teach me to test my intuitions against your Word and to welcome advice. Keep me from perfectionism and let me savor what you have enabled me to do. Help me say what bothers me and love people as they are. Amen.

ENFP.html:
Your portrait

Of all the types, you are the one most drawn to new ideas. Pleasant, friendly, a good talker, you like being among others, and you often have a wide circle of friends and acquaintances. You use language to attract attention and to entertain, and you thus express your creativity and your offbeat personality. You like telling stories and jokes, making puns. You are irreverent, you talk fast, your language is spiced with humor and metaphors, and you may swear more often than others.

Insatiably curious, you quickly steer conversations, you ask many questions and you try to finish other people’s sentences. You often have an original look, and you dress more for yourself than for others, or to mark your difference. In your private life, you are very sensitive and sentimental, but discreet: you share your deep feelings only with those you know and trust.

You have an enormous number of varied occupations and you often change jobs or careers. You enjoy jobs that let you be creative, spontaneous and turned toward others. You like many activities, but you prefer above all to have a good time with your friends.

You are warm and enthusiastic, often brilliant and full of potential. Your enthusiasm lets you inspire and motivate others far more than other types. You can get yourself out of any situation, especially by talking. You love life and you strive to get the best out of it. You have a range of gifts and talents as wide as it is rare, and you excel at anything that holds your interest. Observers may find you disorganized, but you are actually quite consistent, with a great sense of values that live in you all your life.

You need to focus on your projects, and this is sometimes hard for you. Unlike other extraverts, you need time for yourself, to recharge and to make sure your direction is in tune with your values. Those who manage to concentrate succeed in their projects. Others fail because they never finish what they have begun.

You have a strong need to be loved. Sometimes, especially when younger, you can be overflowing with sentimentality and lack sincerity: you overdo it to be accepted. Once you have learned to gauge this need, you bring out the best in others and you are very much appreciated. You have a remarkable gift: seeing through a personality, intuitively, after very little time. You use it to create alter-ego bonds with those you meet.

Because you live in a world of opportunities, the details of daily life seem trivial to you. You give them little importance and you regularly forget them. When you have to get down to them, you have little fun. This casualness can frustrate your family.

You often perceive the truth about a person or a situation quickly, but when you convert this perception into a judgment, you can draw wrong conclusions. Because you often share your interpretation, you can hurt, which is the opposite of your intention. Those of you who turn out badly can become skillful manipulators, thanks to their sense of timing and their sharp tongue, but most do not abuse this talent so as not to damage their values.

You have a keen sense of the future: you guess where the wind will blow, with penetrating intuitions. Your creativity is great, often paired with an artistic taste. You are expansive, sometimes too much. You like being reassured about yourself, which pushes you to seduction, to seduce as well as to be seduced. You cannot stand conflicts and you avoid them as much as possible, even at the cost of sacrificing yourself: seeing discord costs you more than the sacrifice.

At the design stage, you can drown in a crowd of possible choices, consider all kinds of solutions without choosing one, and put the decision off until later. When you decide, your decision may lack precise facts. At the implementation stage, you may lack continuity, and those who followed you for your dynamism risk being frustrated, or having to take over themselves.

Often, you take poor care of your body and you neglect your health. You tend to eat too much, or not enough. Because you are very sensitive and constantly on the alert, you sometimes suffer from muscle tension.

Your strengths

  • You communicate well and you have a fine intuition for the thoughts and motivations of others.
  • You bring out the best in others, and you are warm and affectionate.
  • You are funny, energetic and optimistic.
  • You seek balanced relationships and you respond greatly to the needs of others.
  • You are usually loyal and devoted.
  • You are very enterprising: many ENFPs create their own business.

Your points of vigilance

  • You can be smothering, and your enthusiasm can distort reality.
  • You take little interest in everyday matters like housework or bills.
  • You may keep up harmful, even hurtful relationships, and you constantly look for the perfect relationship, which makes you change often.
  • You like neither conflict nor criticism, and you accept compromises that betray your values.
  • You do not pay enough attention to your own needs and your health.
  • You get bored easily and you find it hard to reprimand or punish.

Your career

You can generally succeed in all the activities that interest you. Yet you get bored fairly quickly and you poorly follow tasks you have begun through to the end. Avoid professions that demand a lot of routine and detailed tasks. You are best in jobs where you invent new ideas and where you work in contact with others. You do not thrive in positions that lock you into the ordinary and hinder your freedom.

The jobs that suit you: consultant, psychologist, entrepreneur, actor, teacher, counselor, politician or diplomat, writer or journalist, programmer, systems analyst or computer scientist, scientist, engineer, art teacher.

You in love

You take your relationships very seriously, but with an almost childlike enthusiasm and energy. You expect a lot of authenticity and depth and you give a lot of yourself to make it work. You are warm, attentive, assertive, devoted, very invested in the well-being of the relationship. You are enthusiastic, idealistic, focused on the feelings of others and very flexible. You use creativity and humor to embellish the relationship, and you are deeply loyal and faithful.

Your first point of tension is the difficulty of ending toxic relationships. You take all the problems on your shoulders and you take on responsibilities that are not yours. Because you are a perfectionist, you do not like defeat and you cling to negative situations. When you leave them, you often think the failure is your fault and that you could have saved the relationship.

Another point of tension: many ENFPs find it hard to stay focused on a relationship over the long term, and long-term faithfulness is not always obvious. You are attracted by the wide spectrum of possibilities and you easily fantasize about situations that seem more enviable, which is rarely the case. If your partner does not like new experiences or does not share your idealism, you get bored, and a bored ENFP is very unhappy and may leave the relationship if the problem is not solved quickly. You also have the habit of often asking your partner where their feelings stand, which can become distressing.

In intimacy, you are perfectionist, playful and affectionate. Your world of fantasy makes you a creative lover, and you see intimacy as a joyful way of expressing the couple’s love. You need a lot of recognition and to be regularly reassured about your charm. You like compliments and you love pleasing the other.

You do not like conflict and you are rather closed to criticism. You are convinced that any criticism targets your whole character, and you take it very badly. You tend to sweep subjects of tension under the rug and to accept compromises that betray your values. But problems do not dissolve this way. Conflict situations are not the end of the world. They are normal and can even contribute to the development of a relationship. You will have a balanced relationship with INTJs or INFJs.

You as a parent

You take your role as a parent to heart and you are also very playful. A child lives in you, and you have enormous fun with your children. You do not lose sight of your values and you strive to pass them on in a pleasant and positive environment.

You can be inconsistent: you switch without warning from the role of best buddy to that of the punishing parent. You wish to be your children’s best friend, but if one of your values is touched, you return to a strict role so that they become aware of their mistakes. This inconsistency can confuse and frustrate them. Your children generally feel loved, but your enthusiasm and your love can smother them, especially in public. Your imagination creates for them an entertaining, dynamic and bubbling environment.

You as a friend

You are warm, sociable and at ease with the desires of others. You have a lot of energy and you are very funny. You find great satisfaction in helping and supporting, and you like authenticity in relationships. Your peers see you as very loving, reliable and generous. At work, you get along with a great variety of people and you strongly feel their aspirations. Getting along is easier with those whose Feeling takes precedence over Thinking, because the latter do not always connect with your spirit. You can feel threatened by those who judge a lot, because you take criticism personally. You are drawn to profiles dominated by intuition and extraversion. You have many friends at every moment of your life, but few will share your aspirations and ideals all your life.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my character, I’m just like that” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Your range of gifts is made for serving: “As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.” (1 Peter 4:10).
  • Your gift of inspiring is a ministry: “Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works” (Hebrews 10:24).
  • Your enthusiasm and joy are blessed: “Serve Yahweh with gladness” (Psalm 100:2) and “A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.” (Proverbs 17:22).
  • Your sincere interest in people is biblical: “each of you also to the things of others” (Philippians 2:4).
  • Your loyalty in friendship has a solid basis: “A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17).

B. Work on your weaknesses with the Word

What you feelWhat the Word saysWhat you do concretely
You scatter yourself, you drown in choices and you do not finish.James 1:8: a double-minded man is unstable in all his ways. / Luke 9:62: no one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back. / 2 Corinthians 8:11: finish what you have begun. / Philippians 3:13-14: one thing I do.Choose one main project per season, and note what is finished. Ask a friend to hold you accountable each week. When a new idea arrives, write it down and wait 48 hours before launching into it.
You seek the perfect relationship, you get bored and you fantasize about elsewhere.Hebrews 13:4-5: honor marriage and be content with what you have. / Philippians 4:11-12: learn to be content. / Proverbs 5:18-19: rejoice in the spouse of your youth.Bring novelty into your current relationship: outings, projects, trips. Replace fantasy with gratitude: write each evening three things you appreciate in the other. Keep your word even when enthusiasm drops.
You have a great need to be loved, to please and to be reassured.Galatians 1:10: serve Christ rather than please men. / 1 Thessalonians 2:4: please God who tests our hearts. / John 15:9: remain in Christ’s love.When you seek a compliment, ask yourself: “Whom am I trying to please?” Feed yourself each day on what God says about you. Do good without being seen.
You avoid conflict and you accept compromises against your values.Ephesians 4:15: speak the truth in love. / Matthew 18:15: go to the person directly. / Acts 5:29: we must obey God rather than men. / Proverbs 12:1: whoever loves correction loves knowledge.Address a small disagreement before it grows. Keep a clear limit on your values. Receive criticism as information, not as a verdict on you.
You draw hasty conclusions about people, your words hurt, and your language can be crude.John 7:24: do not judge by appearance. / Proverbs 18:13: answering before listening is folly. / Ephesians 4:29 and 5:4: no corrupt talk or coarse joking. / Proverbs 12:22: lying lips are an abomination to the Lord.Before voicing your interpretation, ask: “Am I wrong?” Keep your humor without wounding. Replace crude words with words that build up. Never use your charm to manipulate.
You neglect your body and daily life: meals, sleep, bills, housework.1 Corinthians 6:19-20: your body is the temple of the Spirit. / 3 John 2: prosper and be in good health. / Colossians 3:23: do everything heartily. / Luke 16:10: faithfulness in small things.Set regular meal and sleep times. Put bills on automatic payment. Reserve an hour a week for practical tasks, with music.
You switch from buddy to the punishing parent, and you sometimes smother your children.Ephesians 6:4: bring up your children in the Lord. / Matthew 5:37: let your yes be yes. / Hebrews 12:11: discipline yields the fruit of peace.Set a few clear rules with your spouse and keep them every day. Explain the why. Keep the tenderness, but respect their space, especially in public.

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, bring consistency: “let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’” (Matthew 5:37). Say what bothers you instead of avoiding it.
  • As a parent, be consistent: keep the play and add stable rules (Ephesians 6:4).
  • As a friend, your warmth is a gift. Also tell the truth gently when a friend needs it (Galatians 6:1).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Begin each day with the Word and prayer, then choose one single priority to finish.
  • Keep one main project at a time and note what you have completed.
  • Say what bothers you within 24 hours, gently.
  • Eat and sleep at regular times, and move a little every day.
  • Set aside a time of solitude each week to test your directions in the light of the Word.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me joy, curiosity and a taste for people. Teach me to finish what I begin, to stay faithful and to seek your approval first. Give me the courage to tell the truth gently. Help me take care of my body and my loved ones. May my gifts serve your kingdom. Amen.

INFP.html:
Your portrait

You are calm, flexible, easygoing. Your values guide your life and you devote your strength to following an ideal. You move at your own pace toward what matters to you and you rarely let go of your goal. Your humor is very pleasant, but you are poorly known, and some end up forgetting you.

Your inner life is dense. You keep your strongest feelings and convictions to yourself, and you share them only with a few close people. You are probably one of the most idealistic types. You constantly wonder what the meaning of your life is, what your mission is, how you can serve best. Every person you meet, every new piece of knowledge goes through the sieve of your values: does this clarify my route, or change it? At heart, you want to help people and make the world more livable.

In terms of typology, your dominant function is introverted Feeling, supported by an Intuition turned toward possibilities. This explains your psychological flair, your curiosity and your ability to spot opportunities that others do not see.

With others, you listen well and you put them at ease. You express your emotions little, but your attention is deep and you truly want to understand. People sense it, and they confide in you. You do not like conflicts and you will make great efforts to avoid them. When you go through one, you experience it through your feelings: knowing who is right worries you little. Because you handle negative emotions poorly, you may then react illogically. When you are not yourself involved, on the other hand, you make an excellent mediator.

Your values are your engine. You remain flexible as long as they are not touched. If they are trampled, you defend your cause with passion and you can become intractable. As soon as you take on a task, it becomes a cause, and you then take care of every detail until the whole is perfect and coherent. Material daily life, on the other hand, often passes you by: you can go months without seeing a stain on the carpet and yet polish a speck of dust on your planner.

Your values come from your own search, not from rules imposed from outside, which you handle poorly and which you sometimes take pleasure in contradicting. Social recognition matters little to you. Above all you want your feelings and your ideals to be acknowledged. You have an open, imaginative mind, and you learn well when the subject has meaning for you. Abstract logic and objectivity are less your ground. Under stress or anger, you sometimes line up facts, sometimes false, in an emotional outpouring.

When you develop the best of yourself, you do remarkable things for which you rarely give yourself credit. Among your type are people who have set many others in motion.

Your strengths

  • You sincerely seek meaning and you want to improve the lives of others.
  • Your psychological intuition makes you understand others’ motivations and feelings, and you know how to listen.
  • You take time to trust, but once committed, you are fiercely faithful and you love deeply.
  • You encourage, you support, and you respect the freedom and individuality of others.
  • You are creative, flexible, always ready to learn.
  • You express yourself very precisely in writing, even if speaking sometimes bothers you.
  • You calm tensions when you are not caught in the conflict yourself.
  • When a cause is close to your heart, you go to the end of the detail.

Your points of vigilance

  • You are hard on yourself and often dissatisfied. Because preparation motivates you more than execution, you may never conclude.
  • A disagreement can seem like a personal attack to you. Under tension, some INFPs make the other feel guilty to obtain support.
  • You find it hard to say no. You let yourself be overwhelmed, you carry the world on your shoulders, then you blame yourself. You also find it hard to leave a relationship that hurts you, or to reprimand and punish.
  • You are reserved to the point of shyness, you handle it poorly when someone enters your privacy and you sometimes forget to say your love, even though you yourself need to be appreciated.
  • Your idealism can harden to the point of refusing everything that contradicts your values. You then build complicated reasoning to be right.
  • The practical aspects of daily life escape you, and group work is difficult for you, because your demands exceed those of others.
  • You constantly compare reality with your ideal, which feeds dissatisfaction and can paralyze you in your life choices.

Your career

You need a vocation, not just a job. What you do must match your values and make you grow. You are in your place when you can express what you believe in and work for the good of others, without having to go through pure logic.

The jobs that suit you: writer, social worker, teacher or trainer, counselor, psychologist, psychiatrist, musician. There are many writers among INFPs.

You in love

You commit with rare loyalty. You need harmony and warmth to be well, and you take your relationships very seriously. You take time to feel safe. Then, you commit for the long haul. In intimacy, sweet words and the exchange of feelings matter more to you than the act itself, and you often think more of the other’s pleasure than your own. Household and administrative tasks interest you little, but you take care of them when necessary.

You find it hard to talk about your feelings, to the point of forgetting to say your love, but you need it proved to you. When the relationship goes badly, you are deeply affected, you find it hard to talk about it, and you take rejection very badly.

You tend to idealize your partner. This is not necessarily a problem: you work actively to maintain this ideal, and your pride in the other lasts over time. The trap is constantly measuring reality against perfection. One INFP tells that he waited until he was 30 to marry and was still not satisfied, until the day he understood that he could contribute himself to realizing this ideal instead of waiting for it to arrive. For a first date, you take care of every detail: the flowers, the wine, the menu.

Your main obstacle is conflict and criticism, especially with Thinking-Judging (TJ) types, whose frankness can seem aggressive to you. Learn to receive criticism as information about a situation, not as a verdict on you. Remember that an argument is not always your fault and does not mean the end of the relationship. Address the disagreement when it appears, before it grows. You respect the other’s secret garden, you are neither jealous nor possessive and you firmly support their projects. The ENFJ is often the partner with whom you have the best chance of flourishing.

You as a parent

You are a natural parent, warm, encouraging and flexible. You see parenthood as an extension of your values and you respect each child’s personality. You defend them with loyalty and courage. Your point of attention is discipline: you do not like punishing and you gladly leave this role to your partner. If they are absent, make the conscious effort to give your children a firm framework on which they can grow. When your fundamental values are trampled, you do know how to demand a change. Later, your children will remember a patient, devoted and loving parent.

You as a friend

You are cordial and attentive, and you value authenticity. You get along with all kinds of people, but you show your true face only to a few close and lasting friends. You are drawn to those who share your ideals, the Intuition-Feeling (NF) types, and you feel on the same wavelength with the other Feeling types. Getting along is less easy with strongly Thinking and Judging types: you can work with them without necessarily liking them. Your friends describe you as sincere, altruistic, deep, caring and original.

Biblical advice for you

Saying “that’s my personality, I can’t help it” does not match what the Word says. God created you for good works (Ephesians 2:10) and he will complete what he has begun in you (Philippians 1:6). Your temperament is a starting point. It gives you strengths to put at God’s service and fragilities to work on with his help.

A. Put your strengths at God’s service

  • Anchor your idealism in Christ and take action: “be doers of the word, and not only hearers” (James 1:22).
  • Your compassion and your listening serve others: “Bear one another’s burdens” (Galatians 6:2) and “weep with those who weep” (Romans 12:15).
  • Dedicate your pen and your creativity to God. “Write the vision” (Habakkuk 2:2) and “Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord” (Colossians 3:23).
  • Your gift as a mediator is a blessing: “Blessed are the peacemakers” (Matthew 5:9).
  • Your loyalty resembles that of the true friend: “A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17).

C. In your relationships

  • In marriage, do not let the sun go down on an argument (Ephesians 4:26) and say your love with words and gestures.
  • As a parent, “You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.” (Ephesians 6:4). Discipline is part of love (Hebrews 12:11).
  • As a friend, cultivate few friendships but deep ones, and agree to be corrected. “Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.” (Proverbs 27:17).

D. Five practices for growing

  • Each morning, take ten minutes of the Word and silence, then write a few lines in a journal. “Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.” (Psalm 119:105).
  • Choose a trusted brother or sister to be accountable to, who can tell you the truth in love.
  • Each week say one yes and one no clearly, without over-justifying yourself.
  • Finish one thing you have started each week, even imperfectly.
  • Take care of your body (sleep, food) and keep an artistic activity that feeds you.

E. Your prayer

Lord, thank you for giving me a heart that sees and feels. Help me guard it (Proverbs 4:23). Teach me to tell the truth in love, to say no when I must, to finish what I begin and to let you carry what belongs to you. May your Word shape my values, and may my ideal be to resemble you. Amen.
